job: Where have I not looked yet — which addresses, which ports, which ranges, with what flags, and when?

panels.heading: Enumeration matrix — what has actually been looked at, per host
panels.purpose: One row per materialised host, one column per enumeration dimension, so the operator sees in a single glance which hosts are thin and in which direction — without the board ever suggesting what to do about it.
columns: host — `<th class='mxr'>`: `<b>` the IP, `<span class='mono'>` hostname + stage; the IP links to /host?ip=…

full-TCP — mark: `✓` when tcp_full=1 (a 1-65535 run exists); `~` when tcp_rows>0 but tcp_full=0 (scanned, but only a partial range); `·` when tcp_rows=0 (no TCP run the model has seen). title= the tcp_ranges string verbatim

-sV — mark: `✓` when tcp_sv=1 (some TCP run carried -sV/-A); `·` otherwise. Independent of full-TCP: a host can be -sV on top-1000 only, which is exactly the under-enumeration state this column exposes
UDP — mark: `✓` when udp_rows>0 AND udp_ports >= coverage.UDP_FLOOR (100); `~` when udp_rows>0 but shallower than the floor; `·` when udp_rows=0. title= the udp_ranges string verbatim
services — count n_svc, `·` when 0. title='N service row(s) on this host'

surfaces — count n_surf, `·` when 0. title= the comma list of surface kinds from Q2, each suffixed `owes triage` (pack row has service_enum: true), `no gap` (pack row, service_enum falsy) or `not in pack` (no exact-kind row)
web — `apps/paths` as `n_app/n_path` (e.g. `2/15`); `·` only when n_app=0 AND n_path=0; `1/0` is a real and distinct state (app recorded, no paths walked). title='N web_app row(s), M web_path row(s)'
shares — count n_share, `·` when 0
principals — count n_princ, `·` when 0. title='principals attributed to this host (local home_host_id, or a domain anchored here)'

cred tries — n_cred, rendered `.mx ok` when n_cred_ok=n_cred, `.mx bad` when n_cred_ok=0 and n_cred>0, neutral `.mx` in between; `·` when 0. title='N credential_access row(s), M positive'. Counts how many of the vault's creds have been tried here at all
last scan — `scanned_at` from MAX(c.scanned_at), rendered as the raw ISO string; `never` when NULL
panels.empty_state: no hosts in this engagement yet — `yhwach engage <lab> --scope <cidr>` materialises the scope
panels.pack_join: data/service_matrix.yaml via reference._load('services'), built once into `{str(e['kind']).lower(): e for e in reference._load('services')}` and looked up by exact `kind ==` against surface.kind (lower-cased). Never reference.render_pack: verified render_pack('services', k) returns a 0-length string for every one of smb, ldap, kerberos, winrm, ssh, rdp, web. Only `service_enum` is read, and only to label a kind — never to order or rank a row. 44 kinds in the pack; a miss renders `not in pack`, never `no triage owed`.
panels.caveats: (1) scan_coverage.port_count is garbage in the demo DB — 1 or 2 where a real nmap ingest writes 65535/1000/100 (parsers/nmap.py:382 passes cov.port_count). So the UDP `✓` branch is unexercised here: wiki01's udp row has port_count=0 and renders `~`. The ports TEXT ('top-100', '1-65535') is trustworthy; port_count is not. Never render port_count as a number. (2) principal.home_host_id is written by no caller — all four yhdb.add_principal call sites (ingest.py:36,39,120,126) omit it, and it is NULL for all 8 demo principals. The whole column rests on the domain.host_id anchor half, which is why only dc01 shows 8. On an engagement with no LDAP/domain row the column is entirely `·`, and that is honest, not broken. (3) web_app.server/tech and web_path.params/auth_required are never written by ingest_web (ingest.py:86-108), so the web cell deliberately counts rows only and reads none of those columns. (4) Hosts at stage='undiscovered' are excluded; the footer names how many. On the scope-expanded copy that is 245 of 254 rows. (5) Scale is fine: 254 rows x 8 correlated subqueries ran in 1.7 ms; filtered, 0.4 ms. At 60 hosts the matrix is ~60 rows x 11 FIXED columns — unlike _cred_service_matrix, columns do not grow with the estate, so no col_cap is needed and nothing is ever truncated horizontally. (6) credential_access has UNIQUE(credential_id, host_id, proto, port) but no host_id-leading index, so n_cred/n_cred_ok scan; immaterial at engagement scale.

queries.sql:
SELECT h.id, h.ip, h.hostname, h.stage,
       MAX(CASE WHEN c.proto='tcp' THEN c.full_range   ELSE 0 END)  AS tcp_full,
       MAX(CASE WHEN c.proto='tcp' THEN c.version_scan ELSE 0 END)  AS tcp_sv,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN c.proto='tcp' THEN 1 END)                    AS tcp_rows,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN c.proto='udp' THEN 1 END)                    AS udp_rows,
       MAX(CASE WHEN c.proto='udp' THEN c.port_count ELSE 0 END)    AS udp_ports,
       GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN c.proto='tcp' THEN c.ports END, ' ')  AS tcp_ranges,
       GROUP_CONCAT(CASE WHEN c.proto='udp' THEN c.ports END, ' ')  AS udp_ranges,
       MAX(c.scanned_at)                                            AS last_scan,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service  s  WHERE s.host_id=h.id)      AS n_svc,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM surface  u  WHERE u.host_id=h.id)      AS n_surf,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_app  w  WHERE w.host_id=h.id)      AS n_app,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_path p JOIN web_app w2 ON w2.id=p.web_app_id
          WHERE w2.host_id=h.id)                                    AS n_path,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM share    sh WHERE sh.host_id=h.id)     AS n_share,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM principal pr
          WHERE pr.engagement_id = h.engagement_id
            AND (pr.home_host_id = h.id
                 OR pr.domain IN (SELECT d.name FROM domain d
                                    WHERE d.host_id = h.id AND d.type='domain'))) AS n_princ,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credential_access ca WHERE ca.host_id=h.id) AS n_cred,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credential_access ca2 WHERE ca2.host_id=h.id
          AND ca2.result IN ('success','admin'))                    AS n_cred_ok
FROM host h
LEFT JOIN scan_coverage c ON c.host_id = h.id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ? AND h.stage <> 'undiscovered'
GROUP BY h.id
ORDER BY (tcp_full + tcp_sv + (udp_rows > 0)) ASC, h.ip ASC

SELECT h.id, h.ip, GROUP_CONCAT(u.kind, ',') AS kinds, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM surface u JOIN host h ON h.id = u.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
GROUP BY h.id ORDER BY h.ip
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host WHERE engagement_id = ? AND stage = 'undiscovered'

panels.heading: Scope ledger — addresses in scope vs addresses looked at
panels.purpose: One row per CIDR in engagement.scope answering the address half of the question: how big is it, how much of it exists as a host row, and how much of that has ever been scanned.
columns: CIDR — the scope token verbatim, `.mono`; a malformed token renders in `.mx.bad` colours with the text `malformed — engage would reject this`
size — usable addresses, computed by discovery.py's own formula so it matches what scope expansion would create
materialised — host rows whose IP falls inside this CIDR
not materialised — size minus materialised: addresses in scope with no host row at all. This is the 'never looked' number and gets the heaviest visual weight on the row
undiscovered — of the materialised, those still at stage='undiscovered' (a row exists, nothing has touched it)
owes a scan — of the materialised, those with scan_needed=1
with coverage — of the materialised, those with at least one scan_coverage row (i.e. a scan the model actually saw)

touched — of the materialised, those with stage <> 'undiscovered'. Deliberately defined as the complement of undiscovered rather than against a stage allow-list, so an unrecognised stage is never silently dropped from the count
notes — when any host in this CIDR carries a stage outside the schema's eight, a `.chip` listing them, e.g. `off-ledger stage: triaged`
panels.empty_state: engagement.scope is empty — nothing defines where to look. Set it with `yhwach engage <lab> --scope <cidr[,cidr]>`
panels.pack_join: none
panels.caveats: (1) engagement.scope is a comma-separated TEXT mirror of scope.txt; a malformed token is possible in the DB even though `engage` rejects it, so the panel must render rather than raise — scope.scope_networks (scope.py:28-40) silently DROPS bad tokens, which is why this panel re-parses per token itself instead of calling it, so a bad token is visible instead of vanishing. (2) A host row whose IP is in no scope CIDR is real (tunnel-side discovery, operator-added) and must be reported under the table as `N host(s) outside every scope CIDR`, not dropped. Zero in the demo DB, so that branch is unexercised by demo data. (3) At 60 hosts the bucketing is 60 x len(scope) ip_address-in-network tests — trivial. A /16 token yields size=65534 with materialised near zero; discovery refuses to expand anything over /20 (4094 hosts) without --force, so a large 'not materialised' cell is the normal and correct state for a big token, not an error. (4) `off_ledger_stage` exists because the demo DB really does contain stage='triaged', which appears nowhere in the codebase. (5) IPv6 scope tokens parse fine through ipaddress but the size formula (num_addresses-2) is meaningless for them; guard on net.version == 4 and render size as `—` for v6.
panels.reuse: yhwach/scope.py:10-14 (is_ip_or_cidr) and scope.py:17-26 (validate_scope) for the malformed check; mirror the size formula at discovery.py:164-167 rather than re-deriving it. `.card` + plain `<table>` + `<h2 class='sec'>` idiom from _coverage_panel at ui.py:1096-1134. `.chip` CSS at ui.py:184 for the notes cell, `.tile` grid at ui.py:166-171 if the one-CIDR case reads better as tiles than a one-row table. `_esc` at ui.py:538.

SELECT h.ip, h.stage, h.scan_needed,

panels.heading: Scan ledger — every scan the model has seen
panels.purpose: Lists each scan_coverage row as a line of provenance — host, protocol, the port range exactly as nmap reported it, whether the run carried -sV, when it ran, and the argv it came from — plus a footer naming the hosts with no such row at all.
columns: when — scanned_at verbatim, `.mono`. Raw ISO string, not a relative age (see caveats)
host — ip + hostname, linking to /host?ip=…
proto — `tcp` / `udp` as a `.chip`
ports — c.ports verbatim, `.mono`, never reformatted: `1-65535`, `top-1000`, `22,80`. This is the column that answers 'which ranges'
-p- — `✓` when full_range=1, else `·`
-sV — `✓` when version_scan=1, else `·`

source — c.source rendered through _copy_cmd so the operator can lift the argv; when NULL, or when it is a bare token with no whitespace (the demo DB's 'nmap'), render `(argv not recorded)` in `.mono` with no copy button
panels.empty_state: no scan_coverage rows — the model has not seen a single scan. nmap XML reaches it via `yhwach ingest <scan.xml>`; a scan run outside that path is invisible here even if the host rows look populated.
panels.pack_join: none
panels.caveats: (1) c.source is `meta.args` from the nmap XML's run args (parsers/nmap.py:383), so in a real ingest it is a genuine argv line. In the demo DB it is the bare string 'nmap' for all 8 rows, so the copy affordance has nothing useful to copy — hence the explicit degrade branch. Gate the copy button on the source containing whitespace, not on it being non-NULL. (2) Do NOT render port_count: it is 0/1/2 across every demo row where ports says 1-65535 or top-1000. Only `ports`, `full_range` and `version_scan` are trustworthy. (3) UNIQUE(host_id, proto, ports) means a re-run of the same range updates in place rather than appending, and db.py:1011-1018 only ever upgrades version_scan 0->1 and bumps scanned_at — so this ledger is a set of distinct ranges per host, not a true scan history, and scanned_at is the LAST time that range was seen, not the first. Say so in a `.matrix-note` under the table. (4) Do not pass scanned_at through _age_secs for a relative label: it parses `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` only, and discovery.py writes `+00:00`-suffixed stamps — verified _age_secs('2026-10-04T11:31:41+00:00') returns None while the Z form returns a float. Mixed formats coexist in one DB. (5) Scale: rows grow as hosts x distinct ranges, so ~60 hosts x 2-3 ranges is ~150 rows. Cap at 80 rows with a `.hidden-note` reading `+N more scan rows`; do not truncate the footer, which must name every zero-coverage host. (6) The footer excludes stage='undiscovered' on purpose — otherwise a scope expansion makes it 245 names long and says nothing; those addresses are already counted in the scope ledger.
panels.reuse: _copy_cmd at yhwach/ui.py:1065-1075 for the argv cell. `.card` + plain `<table>` + `<h2 class='sec'>` idiom from _coverage_panel at ui.py:1096-1134. `.hidden-note` at ui.py:344-346 for the truncation line, `.matrix-note` at ui.py:369 for the upsert caveat, `.chip` at ui.py:184 for proto. yhdb.coverage_for_engagement at db.py:1032-1043 is the nearest existing helper but selects no `source` column and orders by port_count — do not reuse it here; this panel needs its own SELECT.

SELECT h.ip, h.hostname, c.proto, c.ports, c.port_count, c.full_range,
       c.version_scan, c.source, c.scanned_at
FROM scan_coverage c JOIN host h ON h.id = c.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY c.scanned_at DESC, h.ip, c.proto

SELECT h.ip, h.hostname, h.stage
FROM host h
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
  AND h.stage <> 'undiscovered'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scan_coverage c WHERE c.host_id = h.id)
ORDER BY h.ip

panels.heading: Segments learned in-engagement
panels.purpose: Address space the engagement discovered after scope was written — tunnel subnets and host interface segments — each flagged in-scope or outside-scope so the operator sees new ground and its authorisation status in the same row.
columns: CIDR — the subnet/segment verbatim, `.mono`

scope — a `.chip`: `in scope` (green, _STAGE['done'] family) when scope.in_scope is True; `OUTSIDE SCOPE` (red, `.mx.bad` colours) when False; `label` (neutral) when the value is not an IP or CIDR at all; suppressed entirely with `(no scope set)` when engagement.scope is empty
origin — `tunnel` or `interface` as a `.chip`
via — the pivot/owning host as ip + hostname, linking to /host?ip=…; `(host row missing)` when via_host_id is NULL, which the LEFT JOIN allows
detail — tunnel.kind (ligolo/chisel/ssh_dyn/socat) or host_interface.source (nmap/ip_a/arp/manual)
learned — learned_at verbatim, `.mono`

a scope token? — `✓` when this CIDR appears as its own token in engagement.scope, `·` when it does not. Distinguishes 'inside an existing scope token' from 'is itself a scope token' — the second is what tells the operator the written scope has not caught up with what the engagement learned
panels.empty_state: no segments learned beyond the written scope — no tunnel and no host interface has named a subnet yet
panels.pack_join: none
panels.caveats: (1) host_interface is EMPTY in the demo DB (0 rows), so the interface arm of the UNION is unverified against real data — only its SQL shape is checked. A dual-homed host is the normal source of those rows, so the panel will be tunnel-only on most runs. (2) host_interface.segment is documented as 'CIDR or label' and may legitimately hold 'edge' rather than a CIDR; scope.in_scope (scope.py:42-55) returns False for any non-IP target, so rendering that as `OUTSIDE SCOPE` would be a lie. Pre-check with scope.is_ip_or_cidr. (3) scope.in_scope returns True when engagement.scope is empty — so with no scope set, every learned segment would render `in scope`. Suppress the chip in that case rather than claiming authorisation the DB cannot support. (4) tunnel has UNIQUE(engagement_id, via_host_id, subnet) and via_host_id is nullable, hence the LEFT JOIN. tunnel.kind is a soft enum, so render whatever is stored. (5) The panel states reachability and authorisation; it must not suggest scanning the new subnet — no command, no copy button, no ordering by 'interest'. (6) Scale: rows grow with pivots and interfaces, a handful even on a large estate; no cap needed.
panels.reuse: `.chip` CSS at yhwach/ui.py:184; the tunnel-subnet read pattern already in _network_map at ui.py:1361-1368 (it joins tunnel -> host and renders t['kind'] / t['subnet']); `.card` + `<table>` + `<h2 class='sec'>` idiom from _coverage_panel at ui.py:1096-1134; `.mx.bad` colours at ui.py:362 for the outside-scope chip; `_STAGE` at ui.py:97-106 for the in-scope green. yhwach/scope.py:42-55 (in_scope) and scope.py:10-14 (is_ip_or_cidr).

queries.sql:
SELECT 'tunnel' AS origin, t.subnet AS cidr, t.kind AS detail,
       h.ip AS via_ip, COALESCE(h.hostname,'') AS via_name, t.created_at AS learned_at
  FROM tunnel t LEFT JOIN host h ON h.id = t.via_host_id
 WHERE t.engagement_id = ?
UNION ALL
SELECT 'interface' AS origin, i.segment AS cidr, COALESCE(i.source,'') AS detail,
       h2.ip AS via_ip, COALESCE(h2.hostname,'') AS via_name, i.discovered_at AS learned_at
  FROM host_interface i JOIN host h2 ON h2.id = i.host_id
 WHERE h2.engagement_id = ? AND i.segment IS NOT NULL AND i.segment <> ''
 ORDER BY learned_at DESC, cidr

panels.heading: Discovery provenance — how each host entered the model
panels.purpose: Counts hosts by discovery_source so the operator can see which intake paths are feeding the world model and which are silent, and spot a cohort that was learned but never looked at.
columns: source — the discovery_source value as a `.chip`: one of scope / nmap / finding / cred / cert_san / operator per the schema comment, or `(unrecorded)` for NULL and blank
hosts — n, the cohort size

still undiscovered — still_undiscovered: of that cohort, how many have never been touched. A large number next to `scope` is the normal post-expansion state; a large number next to `finding` or `cred` means the engagement learned about hosts and never went back to them
owes a scan — owes_scan (scan_needed=1)
with coverage — with_coverage: how many have at least one scan_coverage row
first seen / latest — first_seen and latest_seen verbatim, `.mono`; collapsed to a single cell when they are equal
panels.empty_state: no hosts in this engagement yet
panels.pack_join: none
panels.caveats: (1) discovery_source is NULL for all 9 demo hosts, so on the demo DB this panel is a single `(unrecorded)` row and carries almost no information — honest but nearly empty, which is why it sits last. Do not design it to look impressive on demo data; the scope-expanded run above is the shape to design for. (2) discovery_source is schema v2, added via db.py's _ADDED_COLUMNS rather than being in the original table, so an older DB may lack it; wrap the panel in the same best-effort try/except that _coverage_panel uses at ui.py:1104-1106 and return '' on failure rather than breaking the tab. (3) SUM over a boolean and SUM(EXISTS(...)) both return integers in SQLite — verified. COALESCE+NULLIF+TRIM is needed because a blank string and NULL must bucket together. (4) first_seen formats are not uniform within one DB: discovery.py:46-47 writes datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() -> '+00:00', while ingest paths write the 'Z' form. Render the raw string; _age_secs returns None for the '+00:00' form (verified), so a relative age would read `unknown` for exactly the scope-expanded cohort that dominates this panel. (5) Scale: one row per distinct source, at most ~7 rows at any estate size. (6) The six source tokens are a soft enum in a schema comment, not a constraint, so an unexpected value must render as itself and never be folded into `(unrecorded)`.
panels.reuse: `.card` + plain `<table>` + `<h2 class='sec'>` idiom from _coverage_panel at ui.py:1096-1134, and that function's try/except-and-return-'' guard at ui.py:1104-1106. `.chip` CSS at ui.py:184 for the source token; `.tile` grid at ui.py:166-171 is the alternative if the handful of rows reads better as counters. `.empty` at ui.py:188 for the empty state. `_esc` at ui.py:538.

queries.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(h.discovery_source), ''), '(unrecorded)') AS src,
       COUNT(*)                      AS n,
       SUM(h.stage = 'undiscovered') AS still_undiscovered,
       SUM(h.scan_needed = 1)        AS owes_scan,
       SUM(EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM scan_coverage c WHERE c.host_id = h.id)) AS with_coverage,
       MIN(h.first_seen)             AS first_seen,
       MAX(h.first_seen)             AS latest_seen
FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
GROUP BY src ORDER BY n DESC, src

job: What is actually running in this estate, and what is known about each thing?

panels.heading: AI surfaces — every probe hit, decoded
panels.purpose: Puts every AI-kind surface on screen with its meta_json unpacked: the models the box serves, the MCP tools it exposes, the endpoint that answered, the product version and the auth word — the facts that live only in surface.meta_json and have zero production readers today.
columns: host — `h.ip` bold, `h.hostname` after it in .mono, the whole cell an <a href='/host?ip=…'> into the existing host page (ui.py:715); a stage .badge coloured from _STAGE (ui.py:106) sits beside it. NOTE: demo stages 'triaged' are absent from _STAGE and fall back to #5b626d grey.
port — `sv.port`/`sv.proto` in the `.port .pn` accent-magenta idiom (ui.py:287-291), plus `sv.product` in .pv muted. Renders '—' when service_id IS NULL (a host-level surface).
kind — `s.kind` as a .chip in --accent (ui.py:184).

auth — `s.auth` as a .badge coloured by fact, not judgement: 'none' → #d03b3b, any of bearer/token/cookie/basic → #fab219, 'unknown' → var(--muted). The word itself is always printed, so identity is never colour-alone.

assets — the decoded array keys, as labelled chip groups: `models` → 'models:' + one .chip per element; `tools` → 'tools:'; `paths` → 'openapi:'. Shows the first 8 chips then '+N more' as a .chip.more. Each group prints its count. '—' when the surface carries no array key.

endpoint — the full address assembled from the row: `{meta.scheme or 'http'}://{ip}:{port}{meta.endpoint or meta.registry}`, wrapped in _copy_cmd (ui.py:1065) so the operator can lift the exact URL. '—' when neither key is present.
version — decoded `meta.version`. '—' when absent, and the literal word 'null' is shown as '—' because probe_comfyui writes version=None (probes/ai.py:496-500).
facts — a count: 'N keys' linking (via an anchor) to this surface's block in the Probe facts panel below, so the band stays narrow while nothing is hidden.
seen — `s.discovered_at`, in .mono at .72rem.
panels.empty_state: no AI-kind surface recorded — `yhwach probe` has returned no AI probe hit on this engagement
panels.pack_join: none. This panel is pure DB + the meta decoder. (The per-kind pack lookup is deliberately kept in _surfaces_kind_briefing so the band is never gated on a YAML read.)
panels.caveats: The DECODER is the whole panel, so here are the REAL keys each probe writes, read off probes/ai.py and probes/traditional.py — meta_json is always a flat one-level object from json.dumps(result.meta, sort_keys=True) (cli.py:1675-1681, mcp_tools.py:573-576). ollama: endpoint, models[] (elements can be None — `m.get('name')`, ai.py:72). openai_compat: endpoint, scheme, models[] (None when auth='bearer' — the 401/403 branch omits models, ai.py:92-97). chatbot: endpoint, scheme, http_status. n8n: endpoint, scheme, version, instance_id, auth_method, mfa_enforced (bool), release_channel. mcp: endpoint, tools[] (elements can be None). gradio: endpoint, version. a2a: endpoint, scheme, name. openapi: endpoint, scheme, version, title, paths[] — TRUNCATED TO THE FIRST 20 BY THE PROBE (ai.py:333), so the panel must label the paths group '(first 20)' and never imply completeness. vault: endpoint, scheme, version, sealed (bool), initialized (bool). vectordb: engine (qdrant|weaviate|chroma), endpoint, version (weaviate only). mlflow/langflow/ray/triton: endpoint, scheme, version. comfyui: endpoint, scheme, version — EXPLICITLY None when /system_stats has no comfyui_version. Traditional PORT_KIND path: meta={'product': product} and product is frequently None. jenkins: version (from the X-Jenkins header), scheme. gitea: scheme, version (None when /api/v1/version fails). gitlab: scheme only. web/web_upload: scheme, title (None when no <title>), plus `hint` on web_upload. webapp_products (grafana/keycloak/minio/confluence/teamcity/nexus/sonarqube/superset/metabase/jupyterhub/nextcloud/artifactory/jira): scheme, version (None unless the sig has a `ver` endpoint). — Any key NOT in that map must still render: the decoder iterates the parsed dict, prints known keys in a fixed order, then every remaining key verbatim as `key = value`, so a new probe needs no code change here. meta_json can be NULL (schema.sql:74 allows it) or non-JSON text, so wrap json.loads in try/except and fall back to showing the raw string in .mono. The demo's `registry` key is seeded-only — no probe writes it — so it is handled as an endpoint alias, not as evidence that probes emit it. The demo has NO ollama/mcp/openapi/vectordb/n8n surface at all, so on demo.db this panel shows 3 thin rows and the assets column is '—' throughout; that is the fixture, not the query. panels.purpose: Collapses the whole estate's meta_json into one de-duplicated inventory: each distinct model name, MCP tool name, agent name, vector engine, OpenAPI path and endpoint, with the host:port it was seen on and how many surfaces carry it.
columns: class — `asset_class` as a .chip, one colour per class (model #c05bd8, mcp_tool #e83bb0, agent #ec835a, vector_engine #3987e5, openapi_path #fab219, endpoint var(--muted), app_title var(--muted)). Rows are grouped under a .subhdr per class (ui.py:312-314) so the class column is a label, not a sort key the operator has to scan.
asset — the literal string, in .mono. Never truncated mid-token; an asset over 72 chars is rendered with CSS ellipsis and the full value in a title= attribute.

panels.caveats: This is the one panel that needs SQLite's JSON1 extension (json_valid / json_each). JSON1 is compiled in by default from SQLite 3.38 and is on in every Debian/Kali build, and the harness here is 3.50.4 — but on an unknown engagement host it can be absent, so the panel must run inside try/except sqlite3.OperationalError and fall back to the same aggregation done in Python with json.loads over the plain `SELECT COALESCE(s.meta_json,'{}') …` of panel 1 (about 10 lines, identical output). The key→class map is deliberately a closed list: keys outside it (scheme, http_status, sealed, initialized, mfa_enforced, instance_id, hint, product, version, …) are NOT rolled up here because they are per-surface state, not estate assets — nothing is lost, because _surfaces_probe_facts prints every key verbatim. `registry` is folded into 'endpoint' only because the demo fixture uses it; no probe writes it. Array elements can be JSON null (ollama/openai_compat/mcp build their lists with dict.get, probes/ai.py:72, 96, 288) — those arrive as t='null' and are skipped by the `t IN ('text','integer','real')` filter on the scalar branch but WOULD pass through the explode branch as NULL; the renderer must drop NULL assets. openapi `paths` is capped at 20 per surface by the probe, so this inventory of API paths is a floor, never a complete route list — say so in a .matrix-note under the openapi_path group. GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT …) cannot take a custom separator in SQLite, so seen_on/kinds are always comma-joined; an IP or kind containing a comma would corrupt the split (neither can, in practice). Scale: 67 rows / 2.0 ms at 69 hosts; growth is in distinct asset names, not hosts, so a 60-host estate with many MCP servers could reach a few hundred rows — group-by-class plus a per-class 'first 40' cap with a .hidden-note keeps the page bounded.

  SELECT s.id AS sid, s.kind AS kind, h.ip AS ip, sv.port AS port,
         COALESCE(s.meta_json,'{}') AS mj
  FROM surface s
  JOIN host h ON h.id = s.host_id
  LEFT JOIN service sv ON sv.id = s.service_id
  WHERE h.engagement_id = ? AND json_valid(COALESCE(s.meta_json,'{}'))
),
kv AS (
  SELECT m.sid, m.kind, m.ip, m.port, j.key AS k, j.value AS v, j.type AS t
  FROM m, json_each(m.mj) j
),
asset AS (
  SELECT kv.sid, kv.kind, kv.ip, kv.port, kv.k, e.value AS a
  FROM kv, json_each(kv.v) e WHERE kv.t = 'array'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT kv.sid, kv.kind, kv.ip, kv.port, kv.k, kv.v AS a
  FROM kv WHERE kv.t IN ('text','integer','real')
)
SELECT CASE k WHEN 'models' THEN 'model'  WHEN 'tools'    THEN 'mcp_tool'
              WHEN 'paths'  THEN 'openapi_path'
              WHEN 'endpoint' THEN 'endpoint' WHEN 'registry' THEN 'endpoint'
              WHEN 'name'   THEN 'agent'    WHEN 'engine'   THEN 'vector_engine'
              WHEN 'title'  THEN 'app_title' END AS asset_class,
       CAST(a AS TEXT) AS asset,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ip || ':' || COALESCE(port,'?')) AS seen_on,
       COUNT(DISTINCT sid) AS n_surfaces,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT kind) AS kinds
FROM asset
WHERE k IN ('models','tools','paths','endpoint','registry','name','engine','title')
GROUP BY asset_class, asset
ORDER BY CASE asset_class WHEN 'model' THEN 0 WHEN 'mcp_tool' THEN 1
         WHEN 'agent' THEN 2 WHEN 'vector_engine' THEN 3 WHEN 'openapi_path' THEN 4
         WHEN 'endpoint' THEN 5 ELSE 6 END, asset

This is a statement about the WORLD MODEL's knowledge, not a to-do: 'no -sV' means scan_coverage has a row for this host/proto with version_scan=0; 'no scan row' means scan_coverage has nothing for it; 'undisclosed' means -sV ran and the service gave up no version.

SELECT h.ip AS ip, COALESCE(h.hostname,'') AS hostname, h.stage AS stage,
       sv.id AS service_id, sv.port AS port, sv.proto AS proto,
       COALESCE(sv.product,'') AS product, COALESCE(sv.version,'') AS version,
       COALESCE(sv.cpe,'') AS cpe, COALESCE(sv.banner,'') AS banner,
       (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT s.kind) FROM surface s
          WHERE s.service_id = sv.id) AS kinds,
       (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT s.auth) FROM surface s
          WHERE s.service_id = sv.id AND s.auth IS NOT NULL AND s.auth <> '') AS auths,
       (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(sw.name || ' ' || sw.version) FROM software sw
          WHERE sw.service_id = sv.id AND sw.version IS NOT NULL) AS sw_version,
       CASE
         WHEN sv.version IS NOT NULL AND sv.version <> '' THEN 'banner'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM software sw
                        WHERE sw.service_id = sv.id AND sw.version IS NOT NULL) THEN 'software'
         WHEN (SELECT MAX(sc.version_scan) FROM scan_coverage sc
                 WHERE sc.host_id = h.id AND sc.proto = sv.proto) IS NULL THEN 'no scan row'
         WHEN (SELECT MAX(sc.version_scan) FROM scan_coverage sc
                 WHERE sc.host_id = h.id AND sc.proto = sv.proto) = 0 THEN 'no -sV'
         ELSE 'undisclosed'
       END AS version_state
FROM service sv
JOIN host h ON h.id = sv.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY h.ip, sv.port

panels.heading: Probe facts — surface.meta_json, key by key
panels.purpose: Shows the entire contents of every surface's meta_json, decoded key by key, with keys no decoder knows printed verbatim — so the richest column in the schema becomes readable and a brand-new probe needs zero UI code to show up here.
columns: (one <details class='subnet-fold'> block per surface, not a flat table — the rows above are grouped in Python on `sid`)

summary line — `ip:port` in .mono + the kind as a .chip + the auth .badge + `N facts` in .sn-n (ui.py:341) + `seen` timestamp. Open by default when the tab holds ≤ 12 surfaces, collapsed otherwise; native <details>, no JS (the exact idiom at ui.py:2367-2375).

key — inside the block, a 2-column table: `k` in .mono. A key present in the decoder map is plain; a key the decoder does not know is prefixed with a muted '?' glyph and carries title='key not in the probe decoder — shown verbatim', so an unknown key is visibly unknown but never hidden.

value — rendered by `t`: 'text'/'integer'/'real' → the literal in .mono; 'array' → one .chip per element (JSON nulls dropped, first 20 then '+N more'); 'true'/'false' → the words 'yes'/'no' in .mono; 'null' → '—'; 'object' → the compact JSON in .mono at .66rem (no probe writes a nested object today, so this is defensive only).
empty block — a surface with zero facts renders the single line '(no probe facts recorded — this surface came from a port/product classification, not an HTTP probe)' in .empty.
invalid-JSON block — surfaces from the companion query render their raw meta_json in .mono inside a block headed 'meta_json is not valid JSON'.

panels.caveats: Needs JSON1 for json_each/json_valid, same gate and same Python fallback as _surfaces_asset_rollup (iterate `json.loads(meta_json).items()` over panel 1's plain SELECT and bucket types yourself). Note the boolean encoding: n8n's `mfa_enforced: false` comes back as v=0 with t='false' — NOT as the string 'false' — so the renderer must branch on `t`, not on `v`, or every false boolean silently prints as 0. meta_json is nullable (schema.sql:74), so COALESCE to '{}' is required or those surfaces vanish from the join. Five of the demo's twelve surfaces (mssql, winrm, gitlab, ldap, smb) have meta_json='{}' because they came from the deterministic PORT_KIND / fingerprint path, which writes nothing or only {'product': …} (probes/traditional.py:299-307) — so on the demo this panel is mostly empty blocks, and that emptiness is itself the fact: those kinds were classified by port, not interrogated. The `registry` key in the demo's a2a row is seeded-only; the real probe_a2a writes endpoint/scheme/name (probes/ai.py:300-318), so do not take it as a decoder requirement. openapi `paths` is the probe's first-20 slice (ai.py:333), so the array chip group must be labelled '(first 20)'. SELECT h.ip AS ip, wa.id AS app_id, wa.base_url AS base_url,
       COALESCE(wa.vhost,'') AS vhost, COALESCE(wa.title,'') AS title,
       COALESCE(wa.server,'') AS server, COALESCE(wa.tech,'') AS tech,
       COALESCE(wa.waf,'') AS waf, wa.surface_id AS surface_id,
       sv.port AS port,
       (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT s.kind) FROM surface s
          WHERE s.service_id = wa.service_id) AS kinds,
       COUNT(wp.id) AS n_paths,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wp.auth_required = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_gated,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wp.status BETWEEN 200 AND 299 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_2xx,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wp.status BETWEEN 300 AND 399 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_3xx,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wp.status BETWEEN 400 AND 499 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_4xx,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wp.status >= 500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_5xx,
       SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(wp.params,'') <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_params,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT COALESCE(wp.kind,'other')) AS path_kinds,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT COALESCE(wp.source,'')) AS sources
FROM web_app wa
JOIN host h ON h.id = wa.host_id
LEFT JOIN service sv ON sv.id = wa.service_id
LEFT JOIN web_path wp ON wp.web_app_id = wa.id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
GROUP BY wa.id
ORDER BY h.ip, wa.base_url

SELECT wa.id AS app_id, wp.path AS path, wp.method AS method, wp.status AS status,
       wp.length AS length, COALESCE(wp.kind,'other') AS kind,
       wp.auth_required AS auth_required, COALESCE(wp.params,'') AS params,
       wp.interesting AS interesting, COALESCE(wp.source,'') AS source,
       COALESCE(wp.notes,'') AS notes
FROM web_path wp
JOIN web_app wa ON wa.id = wp.web_app_id
JOIN host h ON h.id = wa.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY wa.id, wp.path, wp.method

SELECT COALESCE(wp.kind,'other') AS path_kind, COUNT(*) AS n,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wp.auth_required = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS gated,
       COUNT(DISTINCT wa.id) AS apps
FROM web_path wp JOIN web_app wa ON wa.id = wp.web_app_id
JOIN host h ON h.id = wa.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
GROUP BY path_kind ORDER BY n DESC, path_kind

panels.purpose: Runs the bundled CVE map against every versioned software row right now and shows three honest outcomes per row: the entries that MATCH, the entries whose product matched but whose version predicate ruled the row out, and the products the map has no entry for — so the operator sees the map's coverage, not just its hits.
columns: (three stacked sub-tables under one .card, each with its own .subhdr: 'matched', 'checked — version not affected', 'no map entry')
matched: host — ip + hostname, linked to /host?ip=…
matched: software — `name` `version` in .mono, with `source` ('nmap -sV' / 'probe' / 'linpeas' …) as a .chip and the service's `kinds` as .chips so an AI-infra hit is visibly on an AI surface.
matched: port — `port`/`proto`, or '—' when the software row has no service_id (true for the probe-discovered ollama row).
matched: cve — `entry.cve` in .mono.
matched: cvss — `entry.cvss` right-aligned tabular-nums, coloured from _SEV (ui.py:98) by band: ≥9 critical, ≥7 high, ≥4 medium, else low. None renders '—'.
matched: affected — `entry.affected` verbatim in .mono (e.g. '<0.1.34', '>=16.1.0,<16.7.2'), so the operator can see exactly which predicate fired.
matched: title — `entry.title`.
matched: exploit — `entry.exploit` in _copy_cmd when present, else '—'. This is the map's own exploit_ref string, quoted, not a suggestion generated by the board.
matched: recorded? — 'in vulnerability' .badge when query (b) has a row with the same (ip, cve), else 'not recorded' in .pv — a statement about whether `yhwach vulns` has been run, nothing more.

not-affected: host / software / cve / affected — same cells, plus a muted 'version outside range' note. This section is the panel's real value on a clean estate: it proves the map knows the product and that this version is out of scope.
no-map-entry: host / software — ip, name, version, and 'no entry for this product in data/cve_map.yaml' in .pv. Lists every versioned software row that no entry's name predicate touched.

panels.pack_join: data/cve_map.yaml, loaded ONLY through vulns.load_cve_map() (vulns.py:36, lru_cache(maxsize=1)). Matching is delegated to vulns._entry_matches_software (vulns.py:97: `entry.product in name.lower()` OR `entry.cpe in cpe.lower()`) and vulns.version_matches (vulns.py:77: comma-AND predicate over <=, >=, <, >, ==, bare-exact and '*'). Neither predicate is reimplemented here. _entry_matches_software is module-private; promoting it to a public name (one line in vulns.py: `entry_matches_software = _entry_matches_software`) is the only writer-side change this tab would like, and it is non-behavioural — the panel works without it by importing the private name.

That is the correct output and it is the reason the panel reports all three buckets: a panel that only showed hits would render completely empty here and tell the operator nothing. vulns._entry_matches_software uses a SUBSTRING test on the product name, and the map contains very short products — 'ray' (3 chars), 'exim', 'runc', 'sudo'. Any software whose name happens to contain 'ray' (an 'Array' appliance, 'X-Ray') would false-positive, so the matched row must always print the matched `entry.product` next to the software name, making the join visible and auditable rather than magic. vulns._ver_tuple drops anything after the first '-' and keeps only the first four numeric groups (vulns.py:65-69), so 'Microsoft SQL Server 2019' becomes (2019,) and 'RELEASE.2024-01-31T20-20-33Z' (the minio predicate) degrades badly — version comparison is coarse by design and the panel should not imply precision. software.cpe is NULL for all demo rows, so the cpe arm of the predicate is untested here; it fires only when nmap -sV recorded a CPE. Note the stored-vs-live divergence proven above: all three demo vulnerability rows carry source='cve_map' and software_id=NULL, and none of their CVEs exists in cve_map.yaml — whereas vulns.enrich writes source='version_match' with software_id set (vulns.py:124-129). This panel reads the live map and reports the disagreement; it does not write, so the vulnerability table is never touched. load_cve_map is lru_cached, so a mid-engagement edit to cve_map.yaml needs a UI restart. It can also raise on malformed YAML — wrap the panel and return '' on failure, as _coverage_panel does (ui.py:1106-1109). Scale: 15,290 predicate tests in 3.4 ms at 69 hosts, so the O(software x map) loop is fine even at 10x; the cap to apply is on RENDERED rows, not on tests — show the first 40 per bucket with a .hidden-note.

job: Who is in this domain, what do I hold, and is it safe to spray?

panels.heading: Domain & spray safety
panels.purpose: States the domain we are working, the DC that serves it, and — never collapsed — the lockout posture of EVERY observed password_policy row, so the operator knows before touching an account whether the sprayer's guard is engaged, disengaged, or blind.
columns: Tile: DOMAIN — `engagement.domain`, or the literal text `UNKNOWN — engagement.domain not set` when NULL. Sub-line: `DC <dc_ip> (<dc_hostname>)` hyperlinked to /host?ip=<dc_ip>; `DC not identified` when dc_ip IS NULL.

Tile: PRINCIPALS — total from (B), sub-line `N users · N groups · N computers`. When (B) returns more than one `dom`, a second sub-line lists each `dom` with its count and an `AD DOMAIN SPLIT` chip (the CORP.LOCAL/corp.local dedupe split — see caveats).

Tile: SPRAY GUARD — the single most load-bearing cell, rendered as exactly one of three never-collapsed states, each with its own colour and its own sentence: (1) `NO LOCKOUT (0)` in --ok green + `every observed policy says threshold 0 — the sprayer's guard will not block`; (2) `LOCKOUT AT <t>` in #fab219 amber + `window <w> min` (or `window UNKNOWN — the proxy counts all-time` when lockout_window_min IS NULL) + `sprayer blocks at <t-1> recorded bad attempts`; (3) `NO ROW AT ALL` in --danger red + the verbatim text `UNKNOWN — guard is NOT engaged`, plus `an SMB/LDAP surface exists but no policy was ever read` when E.ad_surface_kinds > 0.
Policy table col 1 — `state`: the (C) `lockout_state` chip, same three values and same three colours as the tile.
Policy table col 2 — `scope`: `pp.dom`, then `@ host_ip (hostname)` when pp.host_id is set, else the literal `domain-wide`.
Policy table col 3 — `lockout`: `lockout_threshold` verbatim, including a literal `0` and a literal `NULL` — never blanked, never defaulted.
Policy table col 4 — `window`: `lockout_window_min` as `N min`, or `NULL` verbatim.
Policy table col 5 — `min length`: `min_length` verbatim or `NULL`.
Policy table col 6 — `complexity`: `ON` for 1, `OFF` for 0, `NULL` verbatim for NULL.

Policy table col 7 — `guard`: a `GUARD USES THIS` chip on the one row whose `pp.id` equals (D).id; blank on the others. When E.rows_with_lockout > 1 and E.strictest_threshold != D.t, that chip is followed by a #fab219 note: `policies disagree — the guard takes the NEWEST (<D.t>), not the strictest (<E.strictest_threshold>); a host-specific row wins per target host`.
Policy table col 8 — `source / seen`: `pp.source` then `pp.discovered_at` in .mono.
panels.empty_state: no password policy read yet — UNKNOWN, guard is NOT engaged. The lockout threshold is unknown, so nothing here says spraying is safe. (yhwach ingest netexec with --pass-pol output writes this row.)
panels.pack_join: none. Verified: reference._load('services') has NO entry whose `kind ==` 'smb', 'ldap', 'kerberos', 'winrm', 'ssh', 'rdp' or 'web' (only 'mssql' of the identity protocols exists), so neither an exact-kind lookup nor render_pack can enrich this panel. data/wadcoms.yaml DOES key on `tag` (e.g. 'smb-passpol' -> tag 'domain_users') and could be joined, but it is a what-command-to-run pack and joining it would turn this panel into a recommender, so it is deliberately not used.
panels.caveats: db.add_password_policy (db.py:1539) has NO dedupe — it is a bare INSERT. Re-ingesting the same DC's --pass-pol output appends a DUPLICATE row every time, so this table grows and can show the same policy N times; that is why the panel renders every row with its id and discovered_at rather than one 'the policy' line. Policies can disagree: sprayer._lockout_policy picks a HOST-SPECIFIC row over a domain-wide one and newest-wins on a tie, so the single `GUARD USES THIS` chip is correct only for hosts with no host-specific row — the disagreement note covers the rest. lockout_window_min is NULL whenever netexec's output lacks a 'Reset account lockout counter' line, and the sprayer then counts fails ALL-TIME (more conservative), which the tile must say. `engagement.domain` and `dc_ip` are only ever written by cli.py:87 / mcp_tools.py:40, i.e. from the operator's own `yhwach init` arguments — if they did not pass --domain, this tile says UNKNOWN even on a fully-enumerated AD. The `domain` TABLE is NOT a fallback: db.add_domain (db.py:1382) has ZERO callers anywhere in the codebase, so in a real run that table is always empty (the demo DB's 2 rows are hand-seeded). Scale: at 60 hosts this is 5 trivial queries, measured 0.0 ms for the policy query over 4 rows; policy rows scale with ingest count not host count, so a cap is unnecessary — but if policy_rows > 12, render the newest 12 and a .hidden-note (ui.py:344) reading `N older policy rows hidden`.

panels.heading: badPwdCount proxy — recorded bad attempts per account
panels.purpose: Shows, per account, how many failed authentications the DB has recorded on the protocols that feed the AD lockout counter, so the operator can see how much room is left before the sprayer's guard refuses — and can see when the guard's own arithmetic disagrees with the visible facts.
columns: `account` — `identifier` verbatim (the vault's spelling, e.g. `corp\j.varga`), in .mono. Grouped by LOWER(identifier) because the guard compares with LOWER(c.identifier)=LOWER(?), so two vault rows differing only in case are ONE lockout account and must be one row here.

`bad attempts (in window)` — `guard_fails_window` as a plain integer. This is the exact number sprayer._recent_account_fails will return. Header carries the cutoff verbatim: `window: since <cutoff>` or `window: ALL TIME (lockout_window_min is NULL)`.

`headroom` — rendered as one of THREE states, never as a bare signed number: `N left` in --ok green when thr-1-guard_fails_window > 0; `0 left — the guard WILL block the next attempt` in #fab219 amber when == 0; `PAST TRIP POINT (−N)` in --danger red when < 0. When no policy row has threshold>0, the whole column is replaced by the literal `no threshold known — guard not engaged` in grey.
`all-time` — `guard_fails_all`, so the operator sees what rolled out of the window. A `+N aged out` note when guard_fails_all > guard_fails_window.

`visible lockout-proto fails` — `lockoutish_fails_all`. When it exceeds `guard_fails_all`, the cell gets a --danger `GUARD BLIND` chip and the row expands to the drill-down rows, each printing `proto=<proto> service_kind=<service_kind>`. This is the column that exposes a miscoded `proto`.
`proven` — `wins` (success+admin count); `—` when 0. Context only: an account with a proven success is one whose password is already known good, so its fails mean something different.
`protos seen` — `protos_seen` in .mono, with `(null)` printed verbatim, and the same for `kinds_seen` on a second line. This is the evidence for the GUARD BLIND chip.
`last recorded` — `last_checked` in .mono, `never tried` when NULL.
panels.empty_state: no credential has been tried against anything yet — nothing has touched a lockout counter. (With no recorded attempts this panel cannot tell you an account is safe to spray; it can only tell you yhwach has not sprayed it.)
panels.pack_join: none. The lockout-protocol set is NOT a YAML fact — it is the frozenset in sprayer.py:248, `{'smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp'}`. The panel must import and iterate `sprayer._DOMAIN_LOCKOUT_PROTOS` rather than hard-coding the literal list, so the panel can never drift from the guard it reports on (precedent: _cred_service_matrix at ui.py:2436 already imports sprayer and calls sprayer._protocol_for).
panels.caveats: This is a PROXY, not badPwdCount. The real attribute is never stored: parsers/netexec.py:70-72 matches `badpwdcount:` with a NON-capturing group `(?:badpwdcount:\s*\d+)?` and discards the value, and no other writer records it — so the only evidence available is yhwach's OWN recorded failures. Three consequences the panel must state in a footer: (1) failures made by hand, by another operator, or by the real user before yhwach arrived are invisible, so the true badPwdCount is >= this number and headroom is an UPPER bound; (2) the sprayer counts only `result='fail'` rows it wrote, and sprayer.py:531-540 does NOT cache a blocked attempt, so a blocked attempt never appears here; (3) the window is wall-clock from datetime.now(UTC) at render time, so the same page refreshed 31 minutes later legitimately shows different numbers — print the cutoff so the number is reproducible. The guard trips at `effective >= thr - 1` (sprayer.py:533), one BELOW the threshold, which is why headroom is thr-1-N and not thr-N; getting this off by one would be the whole panel lying. The demo DB writes credential_access.proto='tcp' (the transport) instead of the auth protocol, so the strict guard predicate matches nothing there — real writers do better (db.mark_credential_validated via ingest.py:62 passes proto=s.proto, i.e. 'smb'/'ldap'; sprayer passes its own protocol key), but mixed-provenance rows are clearly possible, hence the GUARD BLIND column. credential_access rows with proto NULL and port NULL exist in the demo (ids 6,7) and count toward `attempts_all` but never toward the guard. Scale: 880 access rows over 60 creds grouped in 1.3 ms; row count is bounded by credentials, not hosts, so no cap — but cap the drill-down to the 20 most recent rows per account with a .hidden-note.
panels.reuse: The guard arithmetic: import sprayer and reuse `sprayer._DOMAIN_LOCKOUT_PROTOS` (sprayer.py:248); mirror `_lockout_policy` (sprayer.py:251) and `_recent_account_fails` (sprayer.py:269) rather than re-deriving them — the existing precedent for a ui.py panel importing sprayer is _cred_service_matrix at ui.py:2436. Markup: `.card` (ui.py:176) + plain `table` (ui.py:177-180). Three-state headroom chips: `.chip` (ui.py:184) with the `color:X;background:X22` idiom from _tag_chips (ui.py:86). Severity colours: `_SEV` (ui.py:95) for the amber/red. Drill-down rows: the `.sprayfeed` list already built for exactly this shape (CSS ui.py:371-382, renderer _spray_feed at ui.py:2533) — reuse `.sprayfeed li` with its `.sp.bad` fail badge. Footer notes: `.matrix-note` (ui.py:369). Escaping: `_esc` (ui.py:538).

queries.sql:
SELECT LOWER(c.identifier)                                      AS acct_key,
       MIN(c.identifier)                                        AS identifier,
       COUNT(ca.id)                                             AS attempts_all,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ca.result='fail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)         AS fails_all,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ca.result='fail'
                 AND ca.proto IN ('smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                               AS guard_fails_all,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ca.result='fail'
                 AND ca.proto IN ('smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp')
                 AND (?1 IS NULL OR ca.checked_at >= ?1)
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                               AS guard_fails_window,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ca.result='fail'
                 AND (LOWER(IFNULL(ca.proto,''))        IN ('smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp')
                   OR LOWER(IFNULL(ca.service_kind,'')) IN ('smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp'))
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                               AS lockoutish_fails_all,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ca.result IN ('success','admin') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wins,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT IFNULL(ca.proto,'(null)'))          AS protos_seen,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT IFNULL(ca.service_kind,'(null)'))   AS kinds_seen,
       MAX(ca.checked_at)                                        AS last_checked
FROM credential c
LEFT JOIN credential_access ca
       ON ca.credential_id = c.id AND ca.engagement_id = c.engagement_id
WHERE c.engagement_id = ?2
GROUP BY LOWER(c.identifier)
ORDER BY guard_fails_window DESC, lockoutish_fails_all DESC, acct_key

SELECT c.identifier, ca.proto, ca.service_kind, ca.port, h.ip, ca.result, ca.checked_at
FROM credential_access ca
JOIN credential c ON c.id = ca.credential_id
JOIN host h       ON h.id = ca.host_id
WHERE ca.engagement_id=? AND ca.result='fail'
  AND (LOWER(IFNULL(ca.proto,''))        IN ('smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp')
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(ca.service_kind,'')) IN ('smb','winrm','ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp'))
ORDER BY ca.checked_at DESC

panels.heading: Principal roster
panels.purpose: Puts every known account, group and computer on one screen with the one field nothing in yhwach renders today — the full AD description text, where passwords get parked — alongside the flags decoded to English, the SPN, the rights held, and whether the vault already holds a secret for that name.
columns: `account` — the first fragment's `name` verbatim, bold, in .mono. Suffixed by a type chip (`user` / `group` / `computer`) and, when `enabled = 0`, a --danger `DISABLED` chip. When `name_rows > 1`, a #fab219 `SPLIT x<n>` chip linking to a details block listing each fragment as `#<id> domain=<domain or NULL> source=<source or NULL>`.
`domain` — the unioned domain values. One value prints plain; two or more print each as a chip plus the literal note `same name, different domain spelling — one account`.

`flags` — one chip per flag token, decoded to the English sentence from the decoder above, title=the raw token. An unmapped token prints verbatim with `(unknown flag)` so a new producer is never silently swallowed. Empty renders as the literal `no flags collected` in --muted, NOT as a blank cell and NOT as 'no flags set'.
`spn` — every unioned `spn` value in .mono, one per line. `—` when none.

`description` — THE FULL TEXT, every fragment's description, unescaped-then-_esc'd, never truncated, never ellipsised. Rendered in a new `.desc` cell (white-space:pre-wrap; word-break:break-word; max-width:34rem) so a 1024-char AD description wraps instead of blowing the table. This is the cell the panel exists for: `Temp pass Welcome2026! until onboarding` and `pw is Spring2026!` are both real verified rows.

`rights` — one chip per privilege from (B): `<right>` + ` on <host_ip>` when host-scoped + ` -> <target>` when a target is set; a NULL host_id renders the literal `domain-wide`. host_ip links to /host?ip=. `—` when none.

`vault` — from (C) matched by bare name: `<identifier>` + a `(<kind>)` chip + a --ok `validated @<ip>` chip when validated_on_ip is set, else an `untried` chip; `no secret stored` when has_secret is 0. The literal `—` when the vault holds nothing for this name. A credential whose bare name matches NO principal (verified: `sa`, `gitlab-pat`) is NOT dropped — it is listed in a footer line `N vault credentials match no known principal: sa, gitlab-pat` so nothing in the vault goes unaccounted for.
`source / seen` — unioned `source` values and the earliest `discovered_at`, .mono, small.
panels.empty_state: no principals collected yet — run BloodHound/SharpHound collection or a NetExec user enumeration and ingest it. Nothing here means nothing is known about the domain's accounts, not that the domain has none.
panels.pack_join: none. The flag decoder is a Python dict local to ui.py, not a YAML pack: the authoritative vocabulary is produced by parsers/bloodhound.py:125-130 (_FLAG_FOR) and :203-217 (_graph_from_sharphound), so the decoder must be reviewed against those two sites, not against data/*.yaml. Verified that reference._load('services') contains no 'ldap'/'kerberos' entry by exact `kind ==`, so no service-pack enrichment is available. data/tags.yaml carries a 'kerberoastable' entry but keys on finding `tag`, not on a principal flag, so it does not join here.
panels.caveats: THE SPLIT IS REAL AND I REPRODUCED IT WITH PRODUCTION CODE. db.add_principal (db.py:1137) dedupes on (engagement_id, name, domain, type); ingest_bloodhound_graph derives the domain from `user@CORP.LOCAL` (uppercase, via parsers/bloodhound.py:_split_name) while ingest_netexec derives it from the SMB banner `(domain:corp.local)` (lowercase), so the SAME account becomes two rows with two halves of the truth. ingest_bloodhound_graph's `resolve()` (ingest.py:116-123) additionally synthesises a domain=NULL principal for any edge endpoint not in g.principals, producing a third fragment (verified: 'DOMAIN ADMINS'/CORP.LOCAL and 'Domain Admins'/NULL). The collapse on (LOWER(name), type) is therefore not cosmetic, and the SPLIT chip must print each fragment's id because the edges panel addresses principals by raw id. Columns that are NEVER written in production, verified by running every writer: `sid` and `rid` (add_principal has no caller passing them — demo.db's values are hand-seeded, a real run shows NULL, so DO NOT give them a column, only a details line); `enabled` (never set to 0 by any caller, so DISABLED will never fire in a real run today — keep the chip, it costs nothing and is correct the day a writer lands); `credential.principal_id` (exists only via the migration at db.py:33, zero writers — this is exactly why the vault join must go through the normalised name). `flags` and `spn` come ONLY from ingest_bloodhound_graph, so a NetExec-only engagement shows `no flags collected` for everything — demo.db has with_flags=0 across all 8 principals, so the flags column is EMPTY in the demo and the panel must look right that way. `description` comes ONLY from ingest_netexec's `desc:` capture, so a BloodHound-only engagement has none. The bare-name join is name-based and can therefore collide: a local `Administrator` and a domain `Administrator` share a bare name and will show each other's vault entry — the vault cell prints the full `identifier` (with its DOMAIN\ prefix) so the operator can see which. Scale: 1300 principals / 60 hosts measured 3.6 ms, but 1300 TABLE ROWS is an unusable page — cap at 120 identities after the sort and emit a .hidden-note `N more principals hidden — full roster`; the sort guarantees every account with a description, an SPN, a flag, a right or a vault hit is above the cap.
panels.reuse: The whole panel is _creds_vault (ui.py:2104) turned inside out: reuse its `.card` + `table` + chip-per-fact structure, its `_opens_cell` chip idiom (ui.py:2131-2152) for the vault column, and its --ok/#856176 validated-vs-untried colour pair (ui.py:2158-2162). Flag chips: `.chip` (ui.py:184) with the `color:X;background:X22` pattern from _tag_chips (ui.py:86-93). Type chips: `_TAG_COL` (ui.py:54) already carries 'tier0'/'domain-admin' colours worth matching. Rights-per-principal grouping: the bulk-query-into-a-dict pattern from _cred_service_matrix (ui.py:2474-2484) and db.list_credential_access (db.py:767), not correlated subqueries. Hidden-row footer: `.hidden-note` (ui.py:344-346). ONE new CSS rule needed: `.desc{white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:34rem}` — the only existing pre-wrap rule is `.report` (ui.py:243) and it is a card style, not a cell style. Escaping: `_esc` (ui.py:538) — mandatory here, descriptions are attacker-adjacent free text.

SELECT p.id, p.name, p.domain, p.type, p.sid, p.rid, p.enabled,
       p.flags, p.spn, p.description, p.source, p.discovered_at,
       hh.ip AS home_ip, hh.hostname AS home_hostname,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY LOWER(p.name), p.type) AS name_rows
FROM principal p
LEFT JOIN host hh ON hh.id = p.home_host_id
WHERE p.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY p.type, LOWER(p.name), p.id

SELECT pv.principal_id, pv.right, pv.target, pv.host_id,
       ph.ip AS host_ip, ph.hostname AS host_hostname, pv.source
FROM privilege pv
LEFT JOIN host ph ON ph.id = pv.host_id
WHERE pv.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY pv.principal_id, pv.right, pv.id

SELECT c.id, c.identifier, c.kind, c.source,
       (c.secret IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.secret) <> '') AS has_secret,
       vh.ip AS validated_on_ip,
       LOWER(CASE
         WHEN INSTR(REPLACE(c.identifier,'/','\'),'\') > 0
           THEN SUBSTR(REPLACE(c.identifier,'/','\'),
                       INSTR(REPLACE(c.identifier,'/','\'),'\') + 1)
         WHEN INSTR(c.identifier,'@') > 0
           THEN SUBSTR(c.identifier, 1, INSTR(c.identifier,'@') - 1)
         ELSE c.identifier END) AS bare
FROM credential c
LEFT JOIN host vh ON vh.id = c.validated_on_host_id
WHERE c.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY c.id

SELECT COUNT(*) AS total,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type='user' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)     AS users,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type='group' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)    AS groups_,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type='computer' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS computers,
       SUM(CASE WHEN description IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(description)<>'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_desc,
       SUM(CASE WHEN spn         IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(spn)        <>'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_spn,
       SUM(CASE WHEN flags       IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(flags)      <>'' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_flags,
       SUM(CASE WHEN enabled=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)       AS disabled
FROM principal WHERE engagement_id=?

panels.heading: Share inventory
panels.purpose: Lists every SMB/NFS share the current principal's rights were tested against, writable ones first and non-default ones ahead of ADMIN$/C$/IPC$/SYSVOL/NETLOGON, so the operator sees the write surface and the interesting shares without reading past the boilerplate.
columns: `access` — a chip in one of five never-merged states: --ok `WRITE` when writable; #199e70 `READ` when readable and not writable; --danger `NO ACCESS` when denied; --muted `(unknown)` when access was NULL/empty, with the literal note `never tested` — a NULL access is NOT the same as no access and must not be drawn as one. The raw `access` string is also printed verbatim in .mono beside the chip (NetExec emits `READ,WRITE`).

`share` — `sh.name` bold in .mono, with a `DEFAULT` chip in --muted when is_default, so default shares are labelled as well as sorted below. `\\<ip>\<name>` is offered via `_copy_cmd` (ui.py:1065) for the UNC path — copy only, no execution.
`proto` — `sh.proto` (`smb` / `nfs`) as a small chip; it changes what the path means.
`host` — `ip` linked to /host?ip=<ip>, with `hostname` in .mono beneath.
`remark` — `sh.remark` verbatim, _esc'd, wrapped (`.desc`). This is operator-visible free text and in the verified demo row it is where `contains cpassword GPP` lives. `—` when NULL.
`source / seen` — `sh.source` and `sh.discovered_at` in .mono, small.

Two sections, not one table: `WRITABLE / NON-DEFAULT` first under its own h2.sec sub-heading, then `DEFAULT SHARES (ADMIN$ C$ IPC$ SYSVOL NETLOGON ...)` in a collapsed native <details> (reusing the `.subnet-fold` pattern) so the boilerplate is present but never in the way.
Footer from (C): `N host(s) expose an SMB surface with NO share rows: <ip list>` — the shares that were never enumerated, stated as a fact, with no suggestion of what to run.
panels.empty_state: no shares enumerated yet. An SMB surface with no share rows means the enumeration has not run, not that the host has no shares.
panels.pack_join: none. Verified: reference._load('services') has no entry with `kind == 'smb'` (and render_pack('services','smb') returns empty by substring match too), so the share panel cannot be enriched from the service matrix. The default-share name set is a literal in the SQL, chosen to match what NetExec actually emits.
panels.caveats: `share.access` reflects the CURRENT principal's rights (schema.sql:507-517) and db.add_share (db.py:1623) OVERWRITES access on re-ingest while keeping the first `remark` — so this panel is a snapshot under whatever credential was used last, and the same share legitimately flips READ -> READ,WRITE when a better cred arrives. There is no history: no column records WHICH principal the access was tested as, so the panel cannot say 'writable as whom' and must not imply it. `access` is NULL whenever NetExec printed no permission column (parsers/netexec.py:150 maps 'NO ACCESS' to None as well, so a genuinely denied share can arrive as NULL and be shown as `(unknown) never tested` — that is the conservative reading and it is correct, but it means `denied` undercounts). The `nfs` path is reachable via add_share(proto='nfs') but no parser produces NFS rows today, so the proto column will read `smb` everywhere in a real run. `remark` contains real non-ASCII — the verified demo row carries U+2014 EM DASH; the page is already `<meta charset='utf-8'>` (ui.py:570) and `_esc` passes it through, so it renders correctly in a browser even though a Windows console mangles it. Scale: 480 rows over 60 hosts in 1.4 ms, but 8 shares x 60 hosts is 480 table rows — cap the writable/non-default section at 60 rows with a .hidden-note, and keep the default-share <details> fully collapsed (its row count is the signal, not its contents).
panels.reuse: `.card` (ui.py:176) + `table` (ui.py:177-180). Access chips: `.chip` (ui.py:184) with the `color:X;background:X22` idiom from _tag_chips (ui.py:86); colours --ok / #199e70 / --danger / --muted all already in :root (ui.py:131-132) and _STAGE (ui.py:98). The collapsed default-share section: the existing `.subnet-fold` native-<details> pattern (CSS ui.py:321-340, used by _host_stage_board at ui.py:2307) — zero JS, which the offline constraint requires. Hidden-row footer: `.hidden-note` (ui.py:344). UNC copy button: `_copy_cmd` (ui.py:1065). Wrapping remark cell: the same new `.desc` rule the roster panel needs. Host links: the /host?ip= pattern from _hosts (ui.py:1987) with `quote` (already imported, ui.py:28). Escaping: `_esc` (ui.py:538).

SELECT sh.id, sh.host_id, h.ip, h.hostname, sh.name, sh.proto,
       COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(sh.access),''),'(unknown)') AS access, sh.remark,
       sh.source, sh.discovered_at,
       CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.name,'')) IN
              ('ADMIN$','C$','D$','E$','IPC$','PRINT$','SYSVOL','NETLOGON','FAX$')
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_default,
       CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.access,'')) LIKE '%WRITE%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS writable,
       CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.access,'')) LIKE '%READ%'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS readable,
       CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.access,'')) IN ('NO ACCESS','NONE') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS denied
FROM share sh JOIN host h ON h.id = sh.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.access,'')) LIKE '%WRITE%' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
         CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.name,'')) IN
              ('ADMIN$','C$','D$','E$','IPC$','PRINT$','SYSVOL','NETLOGON','FAX$')
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
         h.ip, UPPER(sh.name)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS total,
       SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.access,'')) LIKE '%WRITE%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS writable,
       SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(sh.name,'')) IN
             ('ADMIN$','C$','D$','E$','IPC$','PRINT$','SYSVOL','NETLOGON','FAX$')
           THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS non_default,
       SUM(CASE WHEN sh.access IS NULL OR TRIM(sh.access)='' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS access_unknown,
       COUNT(DISTINCT sh.host_id) AS hosts,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM surface s JOIN host h2 ON h2.id=s.host_id
          WHERE h2.engagement_id=? AND s.kind='smb') AS smb_surfaces
FROM share sh JOIN host h ON h.id = sh.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ?

SELECT h.id, h.ip, h.hostname
FROM surface s JOIN host h ON h.id = s.host_id
WHERE h.engagement_id = ? AND s.kind = 'smb'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM share sh WHERE sh.host_id = h.id)
GROUP BY h.id ORDER BY h.ip

panels.heading: Attack-graph edges
panels.purpose: Renders every edge row with both endpoints resolved from their 'principal:<id>' / 'host:<id>' string form into real names and IPs, so the graph yhwach has actually recorded is readable instead of being a column of opaque ids.
columns: `kind` — `e.kind` in the `.edge .k` uppercase outlined style. Rendered verbatim, never remapped to a friendlier word: the operator needs the BloodHound term (AdminTo, MemberOf, CanRDP, PathToDA, DCSync, CredReuse, TunnelReachable, ESC1 ...).

`from` — `src_label` bold, with a type chip from `src_sub` (user/group/computer/host) and, for a host, the `src_ip` in .mono linked to /host?ip=. When `src_resolved = 0`, the cell prints the RAW `src` string verbatim in .mono plus a --danger `UNRESOLVED` chip, and when `src_type` is neither 'principal' nor 'host' the chip reads `UNRESOLVED (unknown node type '<src_type>')`. Never blank, never silently dropped.
`→` — the `.edge .arrow` glyph.
`to` — identical treatment of `dst_label` / `dst_sub` / `dst_ip` / `dst_resolved`.

`confidence` — a chip: --ok for `confirmed`, --ok for `high`, #fab219 for `likely`/`medium`, --muted for `theoretical`, and the raw value verbatim in --muted for anything else, so an unexpected value is visible rather than coerced.
`source / seen` — `e.source` and `e.discovered_at` in .mono, small.

Inventory line above the table from (B): one chip per `kind` reading `<kind> x<n>` — the operator's at-a-glance census of what kinds of edge exist at all. Followed by a --danger line when (C).bad_node_syntax > 0: `N edge(s) have a node id that is neither principal:<id> nor host:<id>`.

NO path-ranking, NO shortest-path-to-DA ordering, NO 'next hop' column. Rows are ordered by confidence then kind then id only; db.shortest_path (db.py:1262) exists and is deliberately NOT called here.
panels.empty_state: no attack-graph edges recorded yet — BloodHound/SharpHound output has not been ingested, or it contained no da_path facts. Note that group membership does NOT arrive as a membership row; see the world-model inventory below.
panels.pack_join: none. Edge kinds are free-text strings written by ingest.py:43 ('AdminTo') and ingest.py:134 (whatever parse_bloodhound_graph produced, today only 'PathToDA'); there is no YAML vocabulary for them and none should be invented, because a kind the panel does not recognise must still render verbatim.
panels.caveats: Only TWO edge kinds have a production writer, which I verified by running the writers: 'AdminTo' from ingest_netexec (ingest.py:43, confidence defaults to 'confirmed') and 'PathToDA' from ingest_bloodhound_graph via the single `da_path` branch of parsers/bloodhound.py:191-193. Everything else named in the schema comment (MemberOf, HasSession, CanRDP, CanPSRemote, CredReuse, TunnelReachable, ESC1, GenericAll) has NO writer today — demo.db's 'MemberOf' and 'CanRDP' rows and its 'high'/'medium' confidences are hand-seeded, so in a real run this table is short and its confidence column reads 'confirmed' throughout. db.add_edge takes confidence='confirmed' as its default and neither production caller overrides it, so the confidence ordering is currently decorative; keep it, it is correct the day a writer sets it. Endpoints are resolved by raw `principal.id`, which interacts with the roster's split: the same human account can be two principal ids, so two edges that look like duplicates may be the same fact against two fragments of one account — the roster's SPLIT chip lists the ids so the operator can tie them together, and this panel should print `#<id>` beside a resolved principal label for exactly that reason. A dangling id resolves to NULL rather than erroring (verified), and `CAST('bogus' AS INTEGER)` yields 0 which matches nothing, so the UNRESOLVED path is safe. `edge` has a UNIQUE(engagement_id, src, dst, kind) so no duplicate rows, but no reverse-edge dedupe: A->B and B->A are two rows and both are shown. Scale: 1202 edges in 4.7 ms, but 1202 table rows is unusable — cap at 150 rows after the sort with a .hidden-note `N more edges hidden`, and keep the (B) kind census uncapped since it is the summary that survives truncation.
panels.reuse: This is the `.edges` / `.edge` / `.edge .k` / `.edge .arrow` block that _attack_path (ui.py:1859) already renders (CSS ui.py:208-215) — reuse it verbatim rather than building a new table; it was designed for exactly `<node> --KIND--> <node>` rows. Node type chips: `.chip` (ui.py:184) with the _tag_chips colour idiom (ui.py:86). Confidence colours: --ok/--muted from :root (ui.py:131-132) and #fab219 from `_SEV` (ui.py:95). Host links: the /host?ip= pattern from _attack_path and _hosts (ui.py:1987) with `quote` (ui.py:28). Kind census chips: the `.sevleg` inline-legend row (ui.py:174) is the closest existing idiom. Hidden-row footer: `.hidden-note` (ui.py:344). Escaping: `_esc` (ui.py:538) on every label AND on the raw src/dst strings.

WITH n AS (
  SELECT e.id, e.kind, e.confidence, e.source, e.discovered_at, e.src, e.dst,
         SUBSTR(e.src, 1, INSTR(e.src || ':', ':') - 1)  AS src_type,
         SUBSTR(e.src, INSTR(e.src || ':', ':') + 1)     AS src_key,
         SUBSTR(e.dst, 1, INSTR(e.dst || ':', ':') - 1)  AS dst_type,
         SUBSTR(e.dst, INSTR(e.dst || ':', ':') + 1)     AS dst_key
  FROM edge e WHERE e.engagement_id = ?
)
SELECT n.id, n.kind, n.confidence, n.source, n.discovered_at,
       n.src, n.src_type, COALESCE(sp.name, sh.hostname, sh.ip) AS src_label,
       COALESCE(sp.type, CASE WHEN sh.id IS NOT NULL THEN 'host' END) AS src_sub,
       sh.ip AS src_ip, (sp.id IS NOT NULL OR sh.id IS NOT NULL) AS src_resolved,
       n.dst, n.dst_type, COALESCE(dp.name, dh.hostname, dh.ip) AS dst_label,
       COALESCE(dp.type, CASE WHEN dh.id IS NOT NULL THEN 'host' END) AS dst_sub,
       dh.ip AS dst_ip, (dp.id IS NOT NULL OR dh.id IS NOT NULL) AS dst_resolved
FROM n
LEFT JOIN principal sp ON n.src_type='principal' AND sp.id = CAST(n.src_key AS INTEGER) AND sp.engagement_id = ?
LEFT JOIN host      sh ON n.src_type='host'      AND sh.id = CAST(n.src_key AS INTEGER) AND sh.engagement_id = ?
LEFT JOIN principal dp ON n.dst_type='principal' AND dp.id = CAST(n.dst_key AS INTEGER) AND dp.engagement_id = ?
LEFT JOIN host      dh ON n.dst_type='host'      AND dh.id = CAST(n.dst_key AS INTEGER) AND dh.engagement_id = ?
ORDER BY CASE n.confidence WHEN 'confirmed' THEN 0 WHEN 'high' THEN 1 WHEN 'likely' THEN 2
                           WHEN 'medium' THEN 3 WHEN 'theoretical' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END,
         n.kind, n.id

SELECT kind, confidence, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM edge WHERE engagement_id=? GROUP BY kind, confidence ORDER BY n DESC, kind

WITH n AS (
  SELECT e.id,
         SUBSTR(e.src, 1, INSTR(e.src || ':', ':') - 1) AS src_type,
         SUBSTR(e.src, INSTR(e.src || ':', ':') + 1)    AS src_key,
         SUBSTR(e.dst, 1, INSTR(e.dst || ':', ':') - 1) AS dst_type,
         SUBSTR(e.dst, INSTR(e.dst || ':', ':') + 1)    AS dst_key
  FROM edge e WHERE e.engagement_id = ?
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS edges,
       COUNT(DISTINCT src_type || ':' || src_key) AS distinct_src,
       SUM(CASE WHEN src_type NOT IN ('principal','host')
                  OR dst_type NOT IN ('principal','host') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bad_node_syntax
FROM n

panels.heading: AD world model — what is collected and what is not
panels.purpose: States, per class of AD fact, whether yhwach holds it (PRESENT with the literal row count), holds none of it although it could (ABSENT), or cannot hold it because nothing writes it (NOT-COLLECTED) — so an empty panel above is never mistaken for an empty domain.
columns: `status` — a fixed-width chip, exactly one of three values, coloured from the existing `_LLM_STATUS_COL` map: `PRESENT` #6bb36b, `ABSENT` #e06767, `NOT-COLLECTED` #5b626d. Derived from the writer string first and the count second, so a hand-seeded or imported DB with rows in an unwritten table is still honestly labelled NOT-COLLECTED.
`fact class` — the `fact_class` string verbatim.

`rows` — the LITERAL integer from `rows_`, always printed, including `0`, and including a nonzero count on a NOT-COLLECTED row (which is the interesting case: `3` next to NOT-COLLECTED means those rows came from somewhere other than a yhwach writer).
`written by` — the `writer` string verbatim. For a NOT-COLLECTED row this is the reason, e.g. `NONE - add_domain has no caller`.

Legend under the card, in the `.matrix-note` style: `[PRESENT] yhwach holds rows for this · [ABSENT] a writer exists but produced nothing yet — the collection step has not run · [NOT-COLLECTED] nothing in yhwach writes this; it will be empty in every real run, so an empty panel above is not evidence about the domain`.

A called-out footnote under the membership row, because this is the trap the tab exists to avoid: `membership: NOT-COLLECTED (N rows). No production writer exists — ingest_bloodhound_graph writes principals, privileges and edges but never a membership row (verified by running it against a SharpHound groups file: 0 rows). Group membership that IS collected arrives as edge.kind='MemberOf' — M such edges. An empty groups view therefore means NOT-COLLECTED, never a flat domain.` M comes from the companion query; when membership_rows and memberof_edges disagree, add `the two sets disagree — they are written by different paths and neither is derived from the other`.
panels.empty_state: no engagement rows at all — nothing has been ingested for this lab yet.
panels.pack_join: none. Every status is derived from a live row count plus an audited writer string that must be re-verified against the codebase, not from any YAML. Deliberately NOT joined to data/tags.yaml even though it carries a `status: live` field per tag, because that field describes a finding-tag pipeline and would be a different claim wearing the same word.
panels.caveats: The writer strings are a hand-audited snapshot of the code as of this spec and WILL go stale — they must be re-checked whenever ingest.py, db.py or parsers/ change, and the panel should carry a one-line footer naming the audit date. The verification method matters: I confirmed each NOT-COLLECTED claim by executing the production writers against a scratch DB and reading the resulting counts, not by grep alone. Four classes are NOT-COLLECTED today and all four were verified this way: `membership` (0 after a SharpHound groups file + a users file + a facts list + full NetExec output), `domain` (0; add_domain has no caller anywhere), `sid`/`rid` (NULL on all 10 real-ingest principals), and `credential.principal_id` (column exists only via the migration list at db.py:33). `enabled=0` is a fifth: no caller ever passes enabled=False, so `disabled accounts flagged` will read ABSENT-or-NOT-COLLECTED forever until a writer lands — it is listed as NOT-COLLECTED on the writer evidence even though its count is 0, which is the stricter and more useful statement. demo.db is misleading on exactly these columns, which is the reason the status is writer-derived: it carries 3 memberships, 2 domain rows and 8 sid/rid values that no real run would ever produce. The ABSENT state is genuinely ambiguous between 'the collection step has not run' and 'the domain has none of these', and the panel must NOT pretend to distinguish them — the legend says so in words. Scale: 15 scalar COUNT(*) subqueries, each index- or table-scan bounded; measured effectively 0 ms at 60 hosts / 1300 principals. Row count is fixed at 15 regardless of estate size, so this panel never truncates and is the one panel that stays readable at any scale.
panels.reuse: This is _llm_coverage_panel (ui.py:2072-2100) with a different row source — copy its structure directly, including its `.card` + flex-row-per-item markup (no <table>), its `min-width:5.4rem;text-align:center` status chip, and its `.matrix-note` legend (CSS ui.py:369). Reuse `_LLM_STATUS_COL` at ui.py:2069 verbatim for PRESENT/ABSENT and add one key for NOT-COLLECTED mapped to its existing UNKNOWN grey #5b626d. Heading: `h2.sec` (ui.py:165). Escaping: `_esc` (ui.py:538). yhwach/audit.py already owns the llm_coverage() status-matrix helper that _llm_coverage_panel calls — put the identity equivalent beside it as audit.identity_coverage(conn, eid) so the writer-provenance table lives next to the existing coverage audit rather than inside ui.py.
