panels.heading: Reach — every tunnel and what it opened
panels.purpose: One row per tunnel: the CIDR it opened, the host it runs on, the pivot tech, which arsenal binary was shipped, when it opened, and how much of the far side has actually been touched — so a tunnel that opened a segment nobody ever swept is a row with zeros, not an absence.
columns: subnet — `tunnel.subnet` verbatim as a bold mono chip. Mask not in (8,16,24) gets a trailing `~` and `title='counts widened to <prefix>*'`, because the host counts in this row are then over-inclusive.
via — `via_ip` + dim `via_hostname` + the stage badge coloured by `_STAGE.get(via_stage, '#5b626d')`. When `via_ip IS NULL`: literal `via host unknown` in `.muted` (tunnel row has no via_host_id).
kind — `tunnel.kind` as a `.chip` (ligolo / chisel / ssh_dyn / socat), neutral `#856176`; this is a soft-enum free-text column, never colour-coded by meaning.

agent — the shipped binary, resolved by `_agent_binary(agent_path)` (spec in `pack_join`): the label in mono, the resolved absolute path as a `title=`, and a state chip — `on disk` (green `#0ca30c`), `MISSING on disk` (red `#d03b3b`), `arsenal_ref pack` (neutral), `unknown arsenal key` (amber `#fab219`), `not recorded` (muted em-dash).
opened — `created_at` rendered as-is (the `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` string), with `_age_secs()` as a dim relative suffix when it parses (`· 2h ago`).

inside — `hosts_inside` as the big number, then `owned_inside` owned / `pending_inside` pending-scan / `ports_inside` open ports as dim slash-separated counts. When `hosts_inside == 0`, the whole cell is replaced by a single amber chip reading `0 hosts discovered — never swept` (this is the 10.30.0.0/24 case in the demo).
coverage — `no_coverage_inside` of `hosts_inside` have zero `scan_coverage` rows, rendered `3/7 no scan recorded`; `0/0` when the segment is empty renders as `—`.
panels.empty_state: no tunnels recorded — every host on this board is reachable directly from the operator. `yhwach tunnel` (or the yhwach_tunnel MCP tool) writes this table; nothing in the scan/ingest path infers a pivot.
panels.pack_join: `yhwach.reference._load('arsenal')` (data/arsenal_ref.yaml), filtered to `entry.get('surface') == 'pivot'` and indexed by exact `entry['name']`. Verified: that filter yields exactly `['chisel', 'ligolo-agent', 'ligolo-proxy', 'svcmon.exe']`. Do NOT call `reference.render_pack('arsenal', query)` — it substring-matches across every value of every entry and returns prose, not a row. Resolution order in `_agent_binary(agent_path) -> (label, path, state)`, which must never raise: (1) treat the string as a `yhwach.arsenal` registry key — `arsenal.get(s)` inside `try/except KeyError`, never `arsenal.resolve()` (resolve raises ArsenalMissing when the file is absent); on a hit, state is `on disk`/`MISSING on disk` from `item.exists()`. (2) basename of the string (handle both `/` and backslash) against the pivot-filtered pack name; state `arsenal_ref pack`. (3) non-empty but unmatched -> label is the raw string, state `unknown arsenal key`. (4) empty/NULL -> em-dash, state `not recorded`. All four branches executed: 'SVCMON_WIN' -> ('SVCMON_WIN', 'D:\git\yhwach\arsenal\svcmon.exe', 'on disk'); 'CHISEL' -> ('CHISEL', '\usr\local\bin\chisel', 'MISSING on disk'); '/tmp/agent/ligolo-agent' -> ('ligolo-agent', '/usr/bin/ligolo-agent', 'arsenal_ref pack'); 'arsenal\svcmon.exe' -> ('svcmon.exe', 'arsenal/svcmon.exe', 'arsenal_ref pack'); 'LIGOLO_AGENT_WIN' -> ('LIGOLO_AGENT_WIN', '', 'unknown arsenal key'); '' and None -> ('—', '', 'not recorded'). No pack lookup is keyed on `tunnel.kind`; there is no such pack, so kind renders verbatim.
panels.caveats: (1) The demo's only tunnel carries `agent_path='LIGOLO_AGENT_WIN'`, which is NOT a registry key — `arsenal._REGISTRY` holds exactly ['CHISEL','LIGOLO_AGENT_LINUX','LIGOLO_PROXY','REVSHELL_GEN_LINUX','REVSHELL_GEN_WIN','SVCMON_WIN'] and `arsenal.get('LIGOLO_AGENT_WIN')` raises KeyError (verified). So the agent column on the demo renders branch 3, `unknown arsenal key`. That is honest output, not a bug to paper over: the Windows ligolo agent's canonical key is SVCMON_WIN and the writer is drifting. Do not special-case the string. (2) `agent_path` is free text, declared as 'yhwach.arsenal key or absolute path' in the schema; both forms are in the wild, hence the four-branch resolver. (3) Host membership is a `ip LIKE prefix||'%'` string prefix, not real CIDR arithmetic. Exact for /8, /16, /24. For /9-/15, /17-/23 and /25-/32 it widens to the enclosing classful prefix and therefore OVER-counts `hosts_inside` (e.g. a /26 tunnel counts the whole /24) — which makes a segment look more explored than it is. The `~` marker and the `title=` are the mitigation; the honest fix, if it ever matters, is a Python-side `ipaddress.ip_network(subnet).__contains__` filter over the prefix-matched candidates, which is cheap because the prefix already narrows the set. (4) IPv6 and any non-dotted-quad `host.ip` never match any prefix and are silently absent from every count. (5) `host.discovery_source` is NULL for all 9 demo hosts, so this panel cannot say *which* hosts were found because of the tunnel; `hosts_inside` is 'hosts whose IP falls inside', nothing stronger. Do not label the column 'discovered by this tunnel'. (6) Scale: one row per tunnel (realistically 0-4) and 5 correlated subqueries per row; measured 0.9 ms at 321 hosts. No truncation needed, ever.
panels.reuse: Markup: the `.card` + `<table>`/`<thead>`/`<tbody>` idiom exactly as `_coverage_panel` builds it (yhwach/ui.py:1096-1135) and `_hosts` (ui.py:1987-2033); `h2.sec` heading; `.chip` and `.badge` classes from the `_CSS` block (ui.py:171-174); stage colours from the `_STAGE` dict (ui.py:103). Helpers: `_esc` (ui.py:538) on every value, `_age_secs` (ui.py:542) for the relative-time suffix, `_STAGE.get(stage, '#5b626d')` for the via-host badge, `urllib.parse.quote` for the `/host?ip=` link exactly as `_pivot_tree_svg` does (ui.py:1424). Arsenal lookup: `yhwach.arsenal.get` / `ArsenalItem.exists` (arsenal.py:193, 57) and `yhwach.reference._load('arsenal')` (reference.py:27). No new CSS class is required; the only addition anywhere in this tab is one amber-chip style, which can reuse `.chip` with an inline colour as `_tag_chips` already does (ui.py:86).

WITH tun AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.subnet, COALESCE(t.kind,'ligolo') AS kind,
         COALESCE(t.agent_path,'') AS agent_path, t.created_at, t.via_host_id,
         CASE WHEN instr(t.subnet,'/') > 0
              THEN CAST(substr(t.subnet, instr(t.subnet,'/')+1) AS INTEGER)
              ELSE 24 END AS mask,
         CASE WHEN instr(t.subnet,'/') > 0
              THEN substr(t.subnet, 1, instr(t.subnet,'/')-1)
              ELSE t.subnet END AS base
  FROM tunnel t
  WHERE t.engagement_id = :eid
), pfx AS (
  SELECT tun.*,
         CASE
           WHEN mask >= 24 THEN rtrim(base,'0123456789')
           WHEN mask >= 16 THEN rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(base,'0123456789'),'.'),'0123456789')
           WHEN mask >=  8 THEN rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(base,'0123456789'),'.'),
                                                 '0123456789'),'.'),'0123456789')
           ELSE base || '~nomatch'
         END AS prefix
  FROM tun
)
SELECT p.id, p.subnet, p.mask, p.prefix, p.kind, p.agent_path, p.created_at,
       vh.ip AS via_ip, COALESCE(vh.hostname,'') AS via_hostname, vh.stage AS via_stage,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host hi WHERE hi.engagement_id = :eid
          AND hi.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%')                                   AS hosts_inside,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host hi WHERE hi.engagement_id = :eid
          AND hi.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%'
          AND hi.stage IN ('foothold','looted','pivoted','done'))           AS owned_inside,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host hi WHERE hi.engagement_id = :eid
          AND hi.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%' AND hi.scan_needed = 1)            AS pending_inside,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service sv JOIN host hi ON hi.id = sv.host_id
          WHERE hi.engagement_id = :eid AND hi.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%')     AS ports_inside,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host hi WHERE hi.engagement_id = :eid
          AND hi.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%'
          AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scan_coverage c WHERE c.host_id = hi.id))
                                                                            AS no_coverage_inside
FROM pfx p
LEFT JOIN host vh ON vh.id = p.via_host_id
ORDER BY p.created_at, p.subnet

panels.heading: Segments — every /24 I know of, and how far into it I have actually looked
panels.purpose: One row per CIDR drawn from three independent sources — host IPs, `tunnel.subnet`, and the comma-split `engagement.scope` — so that a segment reachable through a pivot with zero hosts in it, and a segment inside scope that was never swept, both appear as rows rather than as nothing.
columns: segment — the CIDR label in bold mono. `wide=1` appends a dim `(wide — overlaps the /24 rows)` note, because a /16 row and the /24 rows inside it both appear and their host counts double-count.

reach — `direct` in `.muted` when `reached_via IS NULL`; otherwise the magenta `.chip` `via <ip> (<kind>)` from `reached_via`, with `tunnel_opened_at` as a dim second line. `group_concat` means two tunnels into the same CIDR render comma-separated.
scope — a small `in scope` chip when `in_scope=1`, nothing otherwise. A row with `in_scope=1 AND hosts=0` additionally gets the amber chip `declared in scope, zero hosts recorded`.

stages — a horizontal strip of count chips (the `.hostchip` class from `_host_stage_board`), one chip per distinct stage present, `COUNT` inside, coloured `_STAGE.get(stage)`. An unrecognised stage (anything not in `db.STAGES` + 'blocked') is drawn with a dashed border and `title='stage not in db.STAGES'` instead of being hidden or silently grey. Total `hosts` is printed to the right of the strip so the chips must visibly sum to it.
pending — `pending_scan` / `hosts` as `9/9`, red `#d03b3b` when `pending_scan == hosts and hosts > 0`, amber when partial, muted em-dash when `hosts = 0`.
ports — `open_ports`, plus `hosts_with_surface`/`hosts` as a dim `9/9 classified` suffix. `0` renders as a muted `0` on purpose — zero open ports in a segment holding hosts is a fact, not a blank.

deep — `deep_covered`/`hosts` with the two-cell bar idiom from `_cov_bar` reduced to one green/red block pair: full-TCP **and** -sV on the same `scan_coverage` tcp row. A dim trailing `· N no scan recorded` carries `no_coverage` when it is non-zero.

sweep — the CIDR restated as a command via `_copy_cmd(f'nmap -sn -n {label} -oX sweep_{slug}.xml')` where `slug = label.replace('/', '_').replace('.', '-')`. Rendered on EVERY row with no ordering, scoring or selection — it is the segment's own identity as a shell string, the same idiom `_coverage_panel` already uses. A `wide=1` row gets a dim `(wide CIDR — expect a long sweep)` note; a `reached_via` row gets `(through the tunnel: ligolo routes at L3 once the route is added; chisel/socat need proxychains4)`.
panels.empty_state: no segments — no hosts, no tunnels and no scope CIDRs recorded for this engagement. `yhwach scope` seeds the scope list; nmap ingest and `yhwach tunnel` fill the rest.
panels.pack_join: none. No YAML pack is keyed on a CIDR or a /24, and inventing one would be the recommender this tab is explicitly not.
panels.caveats: (1) The whole panel hangs on string prefix matching, with the same mask honesty limits as `_reach_table`: exact for /8, /16, /24; widened (over-counting) for every other mask; non-dotted-quad and IPv6 `host.ip` values fall through the GLOB guard and key a segment row under their own raw text. (2) A `wide` row genuinely double-counts against the /24 rows it encloses — the probe run shows 10.40.0.0/16 (hosts=1) and 10.40.5.0/24 (hosts=1) as the same host. Do not sum the `hosts` column into a panel total; print the engagement-wide `COUNT(*) FROM host` separately if a total is wanted. (3) The demo has three hosts at `stage='triaged'`, a value absent from `db.STAGES` (db.py:521). `_STAGE` (ui.py:103) has no key for it, so `_STAGE.get` falls back to `#5b626d`, which is also the `undiscovered` colour — three mid-progress hosts currently render identically to 'never seen'. `coverage.ACTIVE_STAGES` and `STARTED_STAGES` also exclude it, so those three hosts are invisible to the whole coverage subsystem. This panel must not silently mis-colour them: the dashed-border treatment in the `stages` column is a requirement, and the tab note should name the count. Separately, adding 'triaged' to `db.STAGES`/`_STAGE`/`_RANK` (or stopping whatever writes it) is a writer-side fix this tab is not gated on but does expose. (4) `scan_needed` is 1 for all 9 demo hosts including the three owned ones — the pending column will read 9/9 on a board where 3 hosts are already looted/pivoted. That is the DB's state, not a query bug; `scan_needed` is only cleared by a full-port ingest. (5) `engagement.scope` is comma-separated free text mirrored from scope.txt; a malformed entry becomes its own segment row with `prefix` = itself + '~nomatch' and `hosts=0`. Visible and harmless. (6) Scale: 10 correlated subqueries per segment, each a full `host` scan on an expression (no usable index — `sqlite_autoindex_host_1` on (engagement_id, ip) cannot serve a LIKE on a computed prefix), measured 10.1 ms at 321 hosts / 8 segments; a 60-host engagement across 6 segments is well under 5 ms, fine against the 3 s poll in `_POLL_JS`. No row cap is needed — segment count is bounded by distinct /24s, not by host count. If a future run ever expands several /16s, cap the rendered rows at 40 with a `.hidden-note` naming the remainder; do not cap in SQL.
panels.reuse: Markup: `.card` + table from `_coverage_panel` (yhwach/ui.py:1096); `h2.sec`; `.chip` / `.badge` / `.mono` / `.empty` from `_CSS` (ui.py:171-177); the count-chip strip reuses `.hostchip` and `.chips` added for `_host_stage_board` (CSS at ui.py:352-358, renderer at ui.py:2307); the trailing truncation footer, if ever needed, reuses `.hidden-note` (CSS at ui.py:375, used at ui.py:2026). Helpers: `_esc` (ui.py:538); `_copy_cmd` (ui.py:1065) verbatim for the sweep column; `_cov_bar`'s green `#2f8f4e` / red `#8f3030` block pair (ui.py:1077) for the deep-coverage cell; `_STAGE` (ui.py:103) for the stage chips. DB: this panel does NOT use `coverage.coverage_score` / `started_gaps` (coverage.py:208, 243) because both are engagement-wide and both exclude `stage='triaged'`; it reads `scan_coverage` directly instead, and `db.coverage_for_engagement` (db.py:1032) is the shape to copy for the join. The `/24` label expression is the SQL twin of `_subnet_of` (ui.py:1653) — keep them textually adjacent so they cannot drift.

WITH RECURSIVE
scope_split(rest, one) AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(scope,'') || ',', '' FROM engagement WHERE id = :eid
  UNION ALL
  SELECT substr(rest, instr(rest,',')+1), trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest,',')-1))
  FROM scope_split WHERE rest <> ''
),
cidr(label) AS (                         -- every CIDR we know about, as text
  SELECT DISTINCT one FROM scope_split WHERE one <> ''
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT subnet FROM tunnel WHERE engagement_id = :eid
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ip GLOB '*.*.*.*' AND h.ip NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.]*'
                       THEN rtrim(h.ip,'0123456789') || '0/24' ELSE h.ip END
  FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid
),
seg AS (
  SELECT label,
         CASE WHEN instr(label,'/') > 0
              THEN CAST(substr(label, instr(label,'/')+1) AS INTEGER) ELSE 24 END AS mask,
         CASE WHEN instr(label,'/') > 0
              THEN substr(label, 1, instr(label,'/')-1) ELSE label END AS base
  FROM cidr
),
pfx AS (
  SELECT label, mask,
         CASE
           WHEN mask >= 24 THEN rtrim(base,'0123456789')
           WHEN mask >= 16 THEN rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(base,'0123456789'),'.'),'0123456789')
           WHEN mask >=  8 THEN rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(base,'0123456789'),'.'),
                                                 '0123456789'),'.'),'0123456789')
           ELSE base || '~nomatch'
         END AS prefix
  FROM seg
)
SELECT p.label AS segment, p.mask, p.prefix,
       (p.mask < 24)                                                        AS wide,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid
          AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%')                                    AS hosts,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid
          AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%'
          AND h.stage IN ('foothold','looted','pivoted','done'))            AS owned,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid
          AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%' AND h.scan_needed = 1)              AS pending_scan,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service sv JOIN host h ON h.id = sv.host_id
          WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%')       AS open_ports,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT h.id) FROM host h JOIN scan_coverage c ON c.host_id = h.id
          WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%'
            AND c.proto = 'tcp' AND c.full_range = 1 AND c.version_scan = 1) AS deep_covered,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid
          AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%'
          AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scan_coverage c WHERE c.host_id = h.id))
                                                                            AS no_coverage,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT h.id) FROM host h JOIN surface sf ON sf.host_id = h.id
          WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%')       AS hosts_with_surface,
       EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM scope_split z WHERE z.one = p.label)            AS in_scope,
       (SELECT group_concat(COALESCE(vh.ip,'?') || ' (' || COALESCE(t.kind,'ligolo') || ')', ', ')
          FROM tunnel t LEFT JOIN host vh ON vh.id = t.via_host_id
          WHERE t.engagement_id = :eid AND t.subnet = p.label)              AS reached_via,
       (SELECT MIN(t.created_at) FROM tunnel t
          WHERE t.engagement_id = :eid AND t.subnet = p.label)              AS tunnel_opened_at
FROM pfx p
ORDER BY (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tunnel t WHERE t.engagement_id = :eid AND t.subnet = p.label),
         p.prefix, p.mask

WITH RECURSIVE
scope_split(rest, one) AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(scope,'') || ',', '' FROM engagement WHERE id = :eid
  UNION ALL
  SELECT substr(rest, instr(rest,',')+1), trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest,',')-1))
  FROM scope_split WHERE rest <> ''
),
cidr(label) AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT one FROM scope_split WHERE one <> ''
  UNION SELECT DISTINCT subnet FROM tunnel WHERE engagement_id = :eid
  UNION SELECT DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ip GLOB '*.*.*.*' AND h.ip NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.]*'
                             THEN rtrim(h.ip,'0123456789') || '0/24' ELSE h.ip END
        FROM host h WHERE h.engagement_id = :eid
),
pfx AS (
  SELECT label,
         CASE WHEN m >= 24 THEN rtrim(base,'0123456789')
              WHEN m >= 16 THEN rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(base,'0123456789'),'.'),'0123456789')
              WHEN m >=  8 THEN rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(rtrim(base,'0123456789'),'.'),
                                            '0123456789'),'.'),'0123456789')
              ELSE base || '~nomatch' END AS prefix
  FROM (SELECT label,
               CASE WHEN instr(label,'/')>0
                    THEN CAST(substr(label,instr(label,'/')+1) AS INTEGER) ELSE 24 END AS m,
               CASE WHEN instr(label,'/')>0
                    THEN substr(label,1,instr(label,'/')-1) ELSE label END AS base
        FROM cidr)
)
SELECT p.label AS segment, h.stage, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM pfx p JOIN host h
  ON h.engagement_id = :eid AND h.ip LIKE p.prefix || '%'
GROUP BY p.label, h.stage
ORDER BY p.label, n DESC, h.stage

columns: Reuses the existing `.netgrid` / `.nethost` markup and the `.subhdr` segment headers from `_network_map` (ui.py:1554-1620) unchanged.

segment header (`.subhdr`) — the /24 label, plus `· N undiscovered hidden` from C3 when non-zero. Headers render even for a segment whose only hosts are undiscovered, so the group is never silently absent.

A service with no surface row shows `product` or `?`. A host with zero services shows the existing hint line: `scanned — no open ports yet`.

triage pointer (NEW, one dim line per distinct surface kind on the card) — the `enum_ref` string from the services pack, looked up by exact kind. Absent kind renders an em-dash; it is a pointer, never ranked and never ordered.

(When some hosts exist but all are undiscovered, keep the existing wording `all N host(s) are undiscovered — run yhwach_scan --pending`.)

Verified exact-kind results for all 9 surface kinds in the demo: chatbot -> enum_ref 'system-prompt leak -> tool/agency map -> injection', ref_pack owasp-llm; mssql -> 'try sa/default-creds; xp_dirtree UNC -> NetNTLMv2 capture', ref_pack datastores; rag -> no enum_ref, ref_pack owasp-llm; a2a -> no enum_ref, ref_pack owasp-llm; gitlab -> no enum_ref, no ref_pack; and web, winrm, ldap, smb are ABSENT from the pack entirely (4 of the 9 kinds present in the demo). The pack holds 44 kinds total. So the triage line must degrade to an em-dash on a miss and to nothing when `enum_ref` is null, and the `ref_pack` value renders as the dim text `yhwach ref <pack>` only when present.
panels.caveats: (1) The dropped-surface bug above is in the code being moved; moving it without the per-service grouping fix carries a verified data-loss defect onto the new tab. (2) Undiscovered hosts are excluded in SQL (`stage <> 'undiscovered'`) rather than filtered in Python, which is the behaviour change that makes a 254-host scope expansion render 9 cards instead of 263; C3 supplies the hidden counts so nothing becomes invisible. (3) `host.role` is NULL for 8 of 9 demo hosts (only dc01 has 'Domain Controller'), so `_derive_role` carries the role line in practice — and it works off `service.product`, which is populated but has `version` NULL and `cpe` NULL for all 11 demo services. Any card design leaning on version or CPE text will be blank. (4) `service.version` is NULL everywhere in the demo, so the `.pv` version suffix renders as a bare product name with a trailing space (visible in the quoted HTML as `nginx `). Strip it. (5) 'triaged' again: 3 of 9 cards get the grey `_STAGE` fallback, visually identical to `undiscovered`. (7) A surface with `service_id IS NULL` (host-level, not port-level) is NOT returned by C2 at all — the demo has none, but the schema allows them and `ux_surface_hosted_no_svc` exists precisely for them. Add a fourth query for host-level surfaces, or state on the card that only port-bound surfaces are listed. (8) Scale: at 60 non-undiscovered hosts this is 60 cards at `minmax(250px,1fr)` — a long page, but the grid is the point and it sits below the two tables that answer the tab's question. Do not paginate; if a cap is ever wanted, cap per segment group with the existing `.hidden-note` idiom. panels.heading: Interfaces — where a host has a second home
panels.purpose: State plainly which hosts hold an address in more than one segment, because those are the only hosts a pivot can be built on — and, when the table is empty, say exactly which command is the sole writer so the operator reads 'nobody recorded this' instead of 'there are none'.
columns: host — `host_ip` + dim `hostname` + the stage `.badge`. Rows for the same host are visually grouped (first row carries the host cell, continuation rows leave it blank).
interface ip — `iface_ip` in mono. When it equals `host_ip` it is the primary address restated; render it dim and append the `primary` chip rather than hiding it.

segment — `segment` when recorded, else the derived `iface_segment` in `.muted` with `title='derived from the interface IP; no segment label recorded'`. A `segment` that parses as a CIDR and disagrees with `iface_segment` gets an amber `label/IP disagree` chip — that is an operator typo and the tree's dual-homed detection depends on it.

crosses — `home_segment` arrow `iface_segment` with a magenta `bridge` chip when they differ, nothing when they match. This is the column that earns the panel: it is the only place the board states which host physically straddles two segments.

opens a tunnel? — the `tunnel.subnet` whose CIDR equals `iface_segment`, if any, as a `.chip`. Blank means 'this host bridges a segment and no tunnel is recorded through it' — a fact, stated, not a suggestion.
mac — `mac` in mono or an em-dash.
source / seen — `source` (`operator`, `nmap`, `ip_a`, `arp`, `manual`) as a dim chip and `discovered_at` as the raw UTC string.
panels.empty_state: no interfaces recorded. This table is written only by `yhwach interface --lab <lab> --host <host-ip> --ip <iface-ip> [--segment <CIDR>] [--mac <MAC>] [--primary]` (and the yhwach_interface MCP tool) — no scan, parser or ingest path ever fills it, so an empty table means nobody typed one, not that no host is dual-homed. Until then the Reach tree marks a bridge from `tunnel.via_host_id` and the `dual-homed` / `pivot` host tags instead.
panels.pack_join: none.
panels.caveats: (1) Empty in every real run to date, and empty in the demo — the panel's whole value on day one is the empty state above, which is why it must name the writer verbatim rather than saying 'none'. If the empty state is softened to 'no interfaces', this panel is worse than not shipping it. (2) Because the table is empty, the Reach tree's bridge mark currently comes entirely from the fallback arms of T5 (`tunnel.via_host_id` and the host tags) — verified: the 'interface' arm returns 0 rows and 10.20.0.31 is marked only via 'tunnel_via' and 'tag'. (3) `UNIQUE(host_id, ip)` means re-recording the same interface updates (COALESCE-merges) rather than duplicating, so `mac`/`segment` can be filled in later by a second call; `discovered_at` keeps the first value. (4) `segment` is free text labelled 'CIDR or label' in the schema — 'edge' and 'dmz' are legal values, so the `label/IP disagree` check must only fire when `segment` parses as a CIDR. (5) Scale: bounded by operator typing, realistically under 10 rows at 60 hosts; no cap, no truncation. (6) `host_interface` has only `sqlite_autoindex_host_interface_1` on (host_id, ip) — fine for this join direction. (7) The panel sits last on purpose: on today's data it is one sentence, and promoting an empty panel above two populated tables would misstate what the board knows.

WITH acc AS (
    SELECT ca.credential_id, ca.host_id, ca.port, ca.proto, ca.result,
           CASE WHEN ca.result IN ('admin','success') THEN 'proven' ELSE 'failed' END AS bucket
      FROM credential_access ca WHERE ca.engagement_id = ?
),
dedup AS (
    SELECT a.* FROM acc a
     WHERE a.port IS NOT NULL OR a.proto IS NOT NULL
        OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM acc b
                        WHERE b.credential_id = a.credential_id AND b.host_id = a.host_id
                          AND b.bucket = a.bucket
                          AND (b.port IS NOT NULL OR b.proto IS NOT NULL))
),
agg AS (
    SELECT credential_id,
           SUM(bucket='proven')                                       AS n_proven,
           SUM(result='admin')                                        AS n_admin,
           SUM(bucket='failed')                                       AS n_failed,
           COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bucket='proven' THEN host_id END) AS n_hosts_proven
      FROM dedup GROUP BY credential_id
)
SELECT c.id, c.identifier, c.secret, c.kind, c.source,
       sh.ip AS source_host_ip, vh.ip AS validated_on_host_ip, c.discovered_at,
       COALESCE(g.n_proven,0) n_proven, COALESCE(g.n_admin,0) n_admin,
       COALESCE(g.n_failed,0) n_failed, COALESCE(g.n_hosts_proven,0) n_hosts_proven
  FROM credential c
  LEFT JOIN host sh ON sh.id = c.source_host_id
  LEFT JOIN host vh ON vh.id = c.validated_on_host_id
  LEFT JOIN agg  g  ON g.credential_id = c.id
 WHERE c.engagement_id = ?
 ORDER BY (COALESCE(g.n_admin,0)>0) DESC, (COALESCE(g.n_proven,0)>0) DESC,
          (COALESCE(g.n_failed,0)>0) DESC, c.kind, LOWER(c.identifier)

      FROM credential_access ca JOIN host h ON h.id = ca.host_id

panels.heading: Spray safety — observed password policy
panels.purpose: Puts the lockout facts the sprayer's own guard reads on the page you open before spraying: the observed policy, and per-account how many bad attempts are already on the clock.
columns: POLICY BAND (from statement A, rendered as a row of `.tile`s inside `.tiles`, one tile per fact so nothing is colour-only): scope — `domain` plus `@host_ip (hostname)` when `host_id` is set, else `domain-wide`; the row is labelled `observed` and carries `title='source=<source> · seen <discovered_at>'`.

lockout threshold — `lockout_threshold` as the tile `.v`. Rendered three ways and only three: an integer when >0; the literal text `none (0)` when exactly 0, because db/schema.sql:481 and sprayer._lockout_policy both read 0 as "no lockout, spraying unconstrained"; `unknown` when NULL.
window — `lockout_window_min` + ` min`, or `unknown` when NULL. `title` states the consequence as a fact: "counters reset after this window; with an unknown window the guard counts all-time".
min length / complexity — `min_length` and `complexity` (1 -> `on`, 0 -> `off`, NULL -> `unknown`) as two small tiles. Facts only; no judgement of whether the policy is weak.

BUDGET TABLE (from statement B, below the band). account — `identifier`, with ` ·N vault rows (kinds)` appended in `.mono` when `n_cred_rows > 1` so it is visible that several secrets share one lockout counter.

bad attempts on the clock — `fails_in_window` as `N` / `thr`, i.e. exactly the two numbers sprayer.py:527-531 compares. `title` names the guard's rule verbatim: "the guard refuses an attempt once this reaches threshold − 1".

attempts the guard still allows — `attempts_left` (= max(0, thr − 1 − fails_in_window)), or `—` when `thr` is NULL. A `0` is rendered in `var(--danger)` with `title='the next domain-auth attempt on this account is refused by the sprayer guard'`. This is arithmetic on observed facts and the exact figure the guard computes — it names no technique and ranks no action.

recorded failures — `fails_guarded_all_time` then `fails_any_proto` as `N guarded / M total`, with `title` = "guarded = on ldap/ldaps/mssql/rdp/smb/winrm, the protocols that feed badPwdCount; total = every protocol". Both are shown because on this database they differ (0 vs 1) and showing only the guarded count would read as "nothing has ever failed".
last failure — `last_fail_at`, or `—`.
panels.empty_state: no password policy observed — lockout threshold unknown, and the sprayer's guard is inactive until one is recorded (yhwach ingest of a netexec --pass-pol run writes it)
panels.pack_join: none. The lockout constants are Python, not YAML, and must be imported rather than retyped: `sprayer._DOMAIN_LOCKOUT_PROTOS` (sprayer.py:248, verified = {ldap, ldaps, mssql, rdp, smb, winrm}) and `sprayer.PROTOCOL_MATCHERS` (sprayer.py:90, verified: the kinds whose reach intersects those protocols are exactly {ntlm, password}). Checked that `reference._load('services')` has no row keyed smb/ldap/ldaps/winrm/rdp — only `mssql` — so a pack join here would silently cover one protocol in six.
panels.caveats:
THIS PANEL IS A MIRROR, NOT A SHARED IMPORT. /identity does not exist yet — the only routes registered today are /, /panel, /map, /mappanel, /vault, /map.svg, /host, /poc, /report, /report.md, /report/full.md (yhwach/ui.py:670-777). So `_spray_safety_band` must be self-contained in ui.py and the /identity tab should call the same function when it lands; do not write it expecting an identity module to import from.
THE DEMO MAKES THIS PANEL LOOK HEALTHIER THAN IT IS, for two independent reasons that must both be in the rendered caveat line, not just this spec: (1) proto='tcp' on all 7 demo credential_access rows means the guarded fail count is 0 where the true count is 2; (2) the demo rows are 2.5h old against a 30-minute window, so the windowed count would be 0 even with correct protos. Render a `.matrix-note`-styled line under the budget table stating "guarded counts only rows whose proto is a domain-auth protocol; rows written with proto='tcp' are not counted" whenever `fails_any_proto > fails_guarded_all_time` for any account. On this database that line fires.
THE GUARD'S OWN BLIND SPOT, which this panel cannot fix and must not pretend to: the sprayer counts badPwdCount from `credential_access` rows it wrote itself. Attempts made outside yhwach (a manual nxc run, a tool the operator drove by hand) are invisible, so `attempts_left` is an upper bound on what is safe, never a guarantee. State that in the band's footnote.
LOCKOUT-BLOCKED ATTEMPTS ARE NOT PERSISTED. sprayer.py:531-544 counts them only in the in-memory `SprayBatch.blocked` and deliberately does not cache them (comment at sprayer.py:518-520), and they are not written to `attempt` either — verified: the only result='blocked' row in the demo `attempt` table is id=10, playbook_rule_id='smb_null_session', reason='signing required', unrelated to credentials. So this band CANNOT show "the guard already refused N attempts". Do not add that column.
`password_policy` has no UNIQUE constraint (db/schema.sql:478-489), so repeated ingests append rows. Statement (A) therefore lists them all with the live one first, matching sprayer._lockout_policy's `ORDER BY (host_id=?) DESC, id DESC` tie-break — except that the band is engagement-wide and so cannot apply the host_id preference. When two rows disagree on threshold, show both and mark the newest `in effect`; the guard will pick per target host, and claiming one global answer would be a lie.
SCALE at 60 hosts: statement (A) returns one row per observed policy (realistically 1-3). Statement (B) returns one row per distinct account with a password/ntlm secret — bounded by the vault, so 10-30 rows. Neither needs a cap. `fails` scans credential_access filtered to result='fail'; at 20 creds × 400 sprayable services the worst case is a few thousand rows, trivially indexed by idx_cred_access_cred.

SELECT pp.id, pp.domain, pp.host_id, h.ip AS host_ip, h.hostname,
       pp.min_length, pp.lockout_threshold, pp.lockout_window_min,
       pp.complexity, pp.source, pp.discovered_at
  FROM password_policy pp LEFT JOIN host h ON h.id = pp.host_id
 WHERE pp.engagement_id = ?
 ORDER BY (COALESCE(pp.lockout_threshold,0) > 0) DESC, pp.id DESC

WITH pol AS (
    SELECT lockout_threshold AS thr, lockout_window_min AS win
      FROM password_policy
     WHERE engagement_id = ? AND COALESCE(lockout_threshold,0) > 0
     ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
),
acct AS (
    SELECT LOWER(c.identifier) AS acct_key, MIN(c.identifier) AS identifier,
           COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS n_cred_rows,
           GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c.kind) AS kinds
      FROM credential c
     WHERE c.engagement_id = ? AND c.kind IN ('ntlm','password')
     GROUP BY LOWER(c.identifier)
),
fails AS (
    SELECT LOWER(c.identifier) AS acct_key,
           SUM(CASE WHEN ca.proto IN ('ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp','smb','winrm')
                     AND ca.checked_at >= ? THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fails_in_window,
           SUM(CASE WHEN ca.proto IN ('ldap','ldaps','mssql','rdp','smb','winrm')
                    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                         AS fails_guarded_all_time,
           COUNT(*)                                            AS fails_any_proto,
           MAX(ca.checked_at)                                   AS last_fail_at
      FROM credential_access ca JOIN credential c ON c.id = ca.credential_id
     WHERE ca.engagement_id = ? AND ca.result = 'fail'
     GROUP BY LOWER(c.identifier)
)
SELECT a.identifier, a.kinds, a.n_cred_rows,
       COALESCE(f.fails_in_window,0)        AS fails_in_window,
       COALESCE(f.fails_guarded_all_time,0) AS fails_guarded_all_time,
       COALESCE(f.fails_any_proto,0)        AS fails_any_proto,
       f.last_fail_at,
       (SELECT thr FROM pol) AS thr, (SELECT win FROM pol) AS win,
       CASE WHEN (SELECT thr FROM pol) IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE MAX(0, (SELECT thr FROM pol) - 1 - COALESCE(f.fails_in_window,0)) END
            AS attempts_left
  FROM acct a LEFT JOIN fails f ON f.acct_key = a.acct_key
 ORDER BY (COALESCE(f.fails_in_window,0) > 0) DESC,
          COALESCE(f.fails_in_window,0) DESC, LOWER(a.identifier)

panels.heading: Credential × Service matrix
panels.purpose: Which (credential, service) pairs have been tried and how they came out — and, distinctly, which pairs can never be tried because no adapter exists for that credential kind against that protocol.
columns: ROW HEADER (`th.mxr`) — `identifier` over `kind · reach N`, where reach = `len(sprayer.PROTOCOL_MATCHERS[kind])` (verified: password 9, ntlm 5, ssh_key 1, api_key 1, token 1, kerberos 0, dpapi 0). `title` lists the protocols. ip:port
`, `title='ip:port/proto'`. Add the hostname to the title.

panels.caveats:
THE JOIN KEY IS THE WHOLE FIX AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC. Today's 4-part key (cred, host, port, proto) resolves 0 of 40 cells on the demo DB — measured above — because `credential_access.proto` is the application protocol as the WRITER saw it while the column header is the protocol as `_protocol_for` RE-DERIVES it, and the two disagree whenever a writer recorded something else (demo: 'tcp'). (host_id, port) already identifies a service uniquely enough — `service` is UNIQUE(host_id, port, proto) with proto only ever 'tcp'/'udp' — so dropping proto from the key is correct, not a loosening. Verified it resolves all 5 anchored rows, and verified it still works on the real shape: tests/test_ui.py:376 seeds proto='winrm' and sprayer.py:565-579 writes the app protocol, both of which the 3-part key handles identically.
NULL-PORT ROWS CANNOT BE PLACED IN THE GRID. Statement (B) filters `port IS NOT NULL` because a row with no port belongs to no column; 2 of the 7 demo rows are this shape (`db.mark_credential_validated` called without a port, e.g. cli.py:587 when the operator typed `--validated-on 10.0.0.5` with no `:port`). Statement (D) exists so those proofs appear as a footnote rather than vanishing. Do not invent a column for them.
COLUMN CAP: 40 (preserved from ui.py:2503). At 60 hosts × ~8 services ≈ 480 services the grid would be 480 columns, so the cap is load-bearing and the `any_positive DESC` ordering is what keeps the interesting columns inside it. Truncation is 0 on this database (10 sprayable services), so the `.matrix-note` truncation branch is NOT exercised by the demo — test it with a synthetic 50-service fixture or it ships unverified. Rows are uncapped (bounded by the vault, 10-30 in practice).
THE LEGEND MUST NOT BE COLOUR-ONLY. `.mx.admin` and `.mx.ok` differ only in background alpha (ui.py:360-361); the glyphs ◉/✓/✗/·/— carry the meaning, which is why `—` needs its own glyph rather than just a dimmer colour.
`_protocol_for`'s product fallback is a substring match (sprayer.py:169-171), so a service with product=NULL on a non-standard port classifies as None and is dropped. `COALESCE(s.product,'')` in statement (A) makes that deterministic rather than a TypeError. 1 of 11 demo services is dropped this way.
SCALE: statement (A) is one GROUP BY over service LEFT JOIN credential_access — at 480 services and a few thousand access rows it is sub-millisecond on SQLite with idx_cred_access_cred. Statement (B) is one GROUP BY over credential_access. Cell lookup is a dict, as today. Rendered cell count is capped at 40 × len(creds).

SCALE IS THE REAL RISK HERE. `credential_access` grows as (creds × services actually attempted): the demo has 7 rows, but a full autospray at 60 hosts — 20 creds × ~400 reachable (service, protocol) pairs — can write several thousand. A flat render is a multi-thousand-row wall. The `<details>` grouping bounds what is painted (one summary per credential, 10-30 of them) but the `<tbody>` markup is still emitted in full. Cap the rows PER GROUP at 50 with a `.hidden-note` footer "showing the newest 50 of N rows for this credential", and add a global `LIMIT` only if a profile shows the markup size hurts; do not cap globally without the per-group footer, or a credential's own failures silently vanish from its own ledger.
`ca.source` is NULL on 2 of 7 demo rows and must render as `—`, not as an empty cell. Real writers always pass one, so a NULL in a real run means the row came from a `db.mark_credential_validated` call that omitted `source=` — worth the `—` being visible rather than papered over.
`ca.proto` is 'tcp' on every demo row rather than the application protocol; the panel prints it verbatim so the demo reads `445/tcp` where a real run reads `445/smb`. `ca.service_kind` is the more informative of the two on this data ('smb', 'ldap', 'mssql', 'rag', 'gitlab') — which is exactly why both columns are rendered.
ALL SEVEN DEMO ROWS SHARE ONE TIMESTAMP, so "newest first" is untestable against the demo for cross-row ordering — the ORDER BY falls entirely to the tie-breaks. The `(ca.port IS NULL) ASC` tie-break IS verified above (it moves access_id 6 and 7 to the end of their groups). Cross-timestamp ordering needs a fixture with distinct checked_at values or it ships unverified.
This panel and `_spray_feed` read the same table and must not become the same panel. The division is deliberate: this one is per-credential, complete, and answers "everything that was ever tried with THIS secret"; the feed is cross-credential, capped, and answers "what happened most recently". If a later edit makes this one flat and newest-first across credentials, the feed becomes its first 12 rows and one of them should be deleted.
No writer change is needed for this panel. Every column it reads is populated by at least one real writer path today.

Do not substitute lower(label): 'proof.txt' slugs to 'proof-txt'. (b) ORPHAN CHAINS ARE MANDATORY, not optional: `poc.scaffold_from_attempts` (poc.py:102-126) keys chains on `attempt.playbook_rule_id`/`technique_id`, never on an objective label, so a scaffolded run produces chains that match no objective row — 6 of them in the enriched copy. Render them in a second `<tbody>` under a `.subhdr` reading 'chains with no matching objective' with the objective/host/steps columns and a '—' in pts/captured, or the panel silently loses every scaffolded step. (c) `objective.notes` is NULL for all 9 demo rows and is not written by any code path I found — do not give it a column; expose it as a title attribute only. (d) obj4-mssql-sa is captured=1 with captured_at NULL: `objective_captured` events exist for only 2 of the 3 captured flags, so captured_at is a nice-to-have, never the captured test — read `objective.captured`. (e) `output_bytes` uses LENGTH(CAST(... AS BLOB)) = UTF-8 bytes (verified: LENGTH('ąćż…')=4 chars, 9 bytes); plain LENGTH() would report characters and under-report real payload size. (f) truncated_steps matches the literal marker `\n...[truncated]` that add_step appends (poc.py:59); a step whose genuine captured output happens to end in that exact string false-positives — acceptable, and it is the only on-DB signal that output was capped. (g) Scale at 60 hosts: objective rows stay in the tens (one per flag), so the table never needs truncation; query (2) scans every event row of the engagement because there is NO index on event(kind) — only idx_event_engagement_ts (schema.sql:520). panels.purpose: One flat audit row per step that is not yet proof: the command is still the scaffold TODO placeholder, there is no stored output, the output hit the 6000-char cap, or the referenced script file is gone from disk.

panels.pack_join: none
panels.caveats: (a) The on-disk check is a `Path(script).exists()` + `.stat().st_size` per script-bearing step, done in Python after the query. It is safe ONLY because /poc is the one page `_shell` renders without a poll_url (ui.py:726-728, comment 'Static (no auto-refresh)'); if anyone later adds polling to this route, this panel turns into a filesystem stat loop on every tick. Put that in a comment above the exists() call. Wrap each stat in try/except OSError and render a grey 'script unreadable' chip — a path under a dead SMB/sshfs mount raises rather than returning False. (b) `script` holds whatever absolute path `poc.save_script` produced on the recording machine (poc.py:34-41, under artifact_dir(db,'scripts')/slug). A DB copied to another box shows every script as MISSING; say so in the `.matrix-note` footer rather than implying the file was deleted. (c) The WHERE clause deliberately over-selects: it pulls in every script-bearing step so Python can test the disk, then drops the ones that are fine. Count the dropped rows and report them in the footer as 'N script(s) verified present' — otherwise a clean run looks like the panel did no work. (d) `no_command` has never fired in practice: `add_step` defaults command='' but both the CLI (`yhwach poc-step`, cli.py:718-751) and scaffold always pass one. It stays in the audit as a cheap invariant; expect 0. (e) The truncated test depends on the exact `\n...[truncated]` suffix and therefore on _OUTPUT_CAP staying at 6000 (poc.py:22). If the cap ever changes, only the chip's label text needs editing — define the marker as a module constant `_POC_TRUNC_MARK = "\n...[truncated]"` next to the panel and interpolate it into the SQL so the two cannot drift. (f) Scale at 60 hosts: rows = steps-with-a-problem, bounded by total steps (tens to low hundreds). Cap the table at 40 rows ordered as returned and append the `.hidden-note` line 'N more step(s) with the same problems — see the per-chain detail below'.

NULL/blank columns: finding.evidence arrives as '' (not NULL) from actions.py:293 (`evidence=f.get("evidence", "")`), so the predicate must be COALESCE(TRIM(...),'')='' to catch both — a plain `IS NULL` would miss the automated path, which is the main one that produces this gap in a real run. All eight demo findings carry evidence, so class 1 shows 0/8; that is the hand-seeded data being kinder than reality.
loot.local_path: the ONLY writer is mcp_tools.tool_add_loot (mcp_tools.py:812-813) where local_path defaults to None, and db.add_loot (db.py:1517-1526) inserts it unchanged. In a real run this class fires often. Both demo loot rows have local_path filled — unrealistically clean; do not tune thresholds against it.
Unwritten tables: task, technique_state, stage_transition, host_interface and lore_denylist_hit are all EMPTY in the demo and none are read here. event holds no poc_step rows at all in demo.db, which is why classes 2, 4 and 5 read 3/3, 0/0 and 0/0 — class 2's 3/3 is the real signal this panel exists to surface, and classes 4/5 were proved on the seeded copy instead.

A finding flipped to 'exploited' would vanish from BOTH the write-up and this denominator — grep shows nothing in the codebase writes 'exploited' today (zero hits for 'exploited' across yhwach/*.py), so it is latent, not live. Say so rather than silently filtering.
Filesystem touch: class 5 is the only panel on the board that does disk I/O. If the board is served from a machine other than the one holding <artifact>/scripts/, every referenced script reads as missing. Skip the check and render the Count chip as `? / N · artifacts dir not reachable` when the first is_file() raises OSError, and skip it entirely when the (5) row count exceeds 200.
Truncation detection is a sentinel match: it keys on the literal suffix '...[truncated]' that poc.add_step appends (poc.py:59). A step whose real output genuinely ends in that string would false-positive; LENGTH is printed alongside so the operator can see 6015 and judge.

The label is a max over stages, so one pivoted host out of sixty reads "after pivoting" while 59 are merely scanned. That is why the histogram line stays directly beneath the heading — the operator audits the word against "foothold=1, looted=1, pivoted=1, scanned=3, triaged=3" in one glance. Do not drop that line to save space.
'blocked' is mapped to rank 1 (scanning), the same as 'scanned', because it is a terminal side-branch, not progress. An engagement where every host is blocked reads "after scanning", which is correct.

SCALE: constant. 895 B at 9 hosts and 895 B at 60 — it is bounded by the number of distinct credential KINDS (7 in the schema: password|ntlm|kerberos|ssh_key|api_key|token|dpapi), not by credentials or hosts. The three panels it replaces are not bounded: _cred_service_matrix grew 3,468 -> 11,808 B from 9 to 60 hosts because its columns are discovered SERVICES (a 60-host estate with 113 services makes a 4-row x 113-column grid; at 256 hosts it is unusable). That unbounded growth is the real reason the matrix must leave the Board, beyond its byte count.
TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF "UNTRIED" AND THE BOARD MUST NOT CONFLATE THEM. `untried` = no credential_access row exists. `tried_no_hit` = rows exist but none succeeded. The demo has untried=0 and tried_no_hit=1, so a single "untried" number would have been wrong here. Note this ALSO disagrees with _creds_vault's own "untried" chip (ui.py:2162-2166), which is driven by `credential.validated_on_host_id` being NULL — by that measure 2 of the 4 demo credentials read "untried" (ids 3 and 4), even though credential 4 (gitlab-pat) has a `success` access row. The strip deliberately uses credential_access, the proven ledger, not the denormalised validated_on_host_id column. Expect the Board's number to differ from /vault's until /vault is brought into line; flag that to its owner.
NO SECRETS, EVER. The strip prints counts and kinds only. `_secret_cell` (ui.py:2127-2143) and the clipboard buttons do not come along. One consequence worth stating: the `reveal`/`--redact` flag now has no effect on the Board.
`last_checked` IS RENDERED RAW as the stored ISO-8601 UTC string, not relative. `_age_secs` (ui.py:542) exists and parses exactly `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`, so a "4m ago" rendering is available — but a relative time on a 3s-polled fragment visibly ticks and draws the eye for no reason. Absolute is the deliberate choice.
`?1` NAMED BINDING: V1 binds the engagement id once via `?1`. sqlite3 supports this; passing a 1-tuple is enough. Do not convert it to eight `?` placeholders without also changing the parameter tuple.
`hosts_opened` COUNTS DISTINCT host_id IN credential_access, which can exceed the number of OWNED hosts — a credential proving against a host does not advance that host's stage. It is not a substitute for the owned count in _tiles.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credential WHERE engagement_id = ?1) AS creds,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT credential_id) FROM credential_access
     WHERE engagement_id = ?1 AND result IN ('success','admin')) AS proven,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT credential_id) FROM credential_access
     WHERE engagement_id = ?1 AND result = 'admin') AS admin_creds,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT host_id) FROM credential_access
     WHERE engagement_id = ?1 AND result IN ('success','admin')) AS hosts_opened,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credential c WHERE c.engagement_id = ?1
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM credential_access a
                      WHERE a.credential_id = c.id)) AS untried,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credential c WHERE c.engagement_id = ?1
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM credential_access a WHERE a.credential_id = c.id)
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM credential_access a2
                      WHERE a2.credential_id = c.id
                        AND a2.result IN ('success','admin'))) AS tried_no_hit,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credential_access
     WHERE engagement_id = ?1 AND result = 'fail') AS failed_pairs,
  (SELECT MAX(checked_at) FROM credential_access
     WHERE engagement_id = ?1) AS last_checked

SELECT c.kind, COUNT(*) AS n,
       SUM(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM credential_access a
                    WHERE a.credential_id = c.id
                      AND a.result IN ('success','admin'))) AS proven
  FROM credential c
 WHERE c.engagement_id = ?
 GROUP BY c.kind
 ORDER BY n DESC, c.kind

panels.caveats:
THE CAP IS A PYTHON SLICE, NOT A SQL LIMIT. started_gaps does the sorting and the gap derivation in Python (coverage.py:211+), so there is no query to attach LIMIT to. Consequence: the FULL computation still runs every 3 seconds for all 56 hosts and only the rendering is capped. The byte saving is real (-38,880 B at 60 hosts) but the CPU saving is zero. If the 3s poll ever becomes CPU-bound rather than payload-bound, this panel is where to look, and the fix is inside coverage.py, not ui.py.
WORST-FIRST ORDERING IS WHAT MAKES THE CAP ACCEPTABLE (rule R5). started_gaps returns worst-first, so the 25 shown are the 25 worst-enumerated hosts and the hidden 31 are the closest to complete. Verify that contract has not drifted before relying on it — if the sort ever becomes unstable, the visible set will churn every 3 seconds.
EVERY SYNTHETIC HOST IN MY 60-HOST CLONE HAS A GAP (56 of 60 rows), because I gave them full-range tcp + version scan but no UDP coverage row. That is realistic — UDP sweeps are the commonly skipped dimension — but it means my measured 71,725 B is close to a worst case for this panel. A real estate with UDP coverage would start smaller and the cap would bite later.
HIGH PER-ROW COST IS STRUCTURAL. `_copy_cmd` duplicating the command (data attribute + text) plus an inline onclick is ~300-400 B per gap. A host with 3 gaps (demo: 10.20.0.60) costs well over 1 KB on its own. Capping at 25 is the only lever available here without touching _copy_cmd, which is shared with other tabs.
STAGE FILTER: started_gaps considers hosts that have been REACHED. The bounding scalar above uses `stage NOT IN ('undiscovered')` and returns 9/60, against 5/56 actual gap rows — the difference is hosts that are fully enumerated and correctly absent.

panels.heading: Standards inventory
panels.purpose: Sits immediately beside the OWASP-LLM matrix and does for every taxonomy family what that panel does for LLM01-10: names all seven families, including the ones at zero, so an absent family reads as "never classified against" rather than as silence. Inventory, not advice — it says which families have proven findings, never which to go test.
columns: count chip — "<N> finding(s)", `.chip`, green #6bb36b when N > 0 and grey #5b626d at zero, `min-width:5.4rem;text-align:center`. Deliberately mirrors the PRESENT/ABSENT/UNKNOWN chip geometry of `_llm_coverage_panel` (ui.py:2096-2098) so the two panels read as one pair.

family — the family name, `.mono`, `min-width:5.5rem`. All seven from `audit._ORDER` (audit.py:62) are always rendered in that fixed order: ATT&CK, ATLAS, OWASP-LLM, OWASP-ML, CWE, CVE, other. Rendering the zeros is the entire point — a missing row would be indistinguishable from a family with no findings.

ids — the distinct `finding.class` values in that family, " · "-joined, first 8 then " +N". `<span class='mono' style='font-size:.7rem;color:var(--muted)'>`. An em-dash when the family is empty. (NOT `class='pv'` — see the CSS note in tab_caveats.)

note (`.matrix-note` below the card) — "<open_total> open finding(s); <unclassified> carry no `class` and land in no family; <not_open> non-open finding(s) excluded. A family at 0 was never classified against — not proof it was tested." That last clause is the anti-recommender guard: it stops a grey zero being read as a to-do.

panels.pack_join: none. No YAML at all — the seven families come from the hardcoded `audit._ORDER` list (audit.py:62) and the `_FAMILIES` regex table (audit.py:27-34), both already in the codebase. OWASP_LLM_TOP10 (audit.py:74-85) is likewise hardcoded and is consumed by the sibling panel, not this one.
panels.caveats:
ON THE DEMO DB THIS PANEL IS ALMOST ALL ZEROS, AND THAT IS A SEED ARTEFACT, NOT A FINDING. W3: `finding.class` holds 'ai','cve','privesc','misconfig','info' — internal category words. `audit._family()` matches none of them, so all 8 land in `other` and six families read 0. The real writers DO emit taxonomy ids (vulns.py:134-136 -> `CVE-…`; ingest.py:75-83 -> `CWE-287/434/284/200/527/530/538`; actions.py:291 -> `LLM01`; mcp_tools.py:765 -> `INFO`), which is why the 60-host clone, seeded with a real CWE-200, correctly produces a populated CWE family. Anyone reviewing the mockup must be told this, or they will read "ATT&CK 0" as a methodology gap when it is a seeding bug. Fixing the seed to use taxonomy ids would make the demo mockup representative.
`INFO` IS A VALID CLASS THAT MAPS TO `other`. mcp_tools.tool_add_finding defaults `cls="INFO"` (mcp_tools.py:765), which matches no family regex. So in a REAL engagement the `other` row collects every operator-recorded finding that was not given a taxonomy id. Expect `other` to be the largest family on most runs. That is honest, and the note line explains it.
SCOPE MISMATCH WITH THE REPORT IS STATED, NOT HIDDEN. findings_by_standard filters `status = 'open'` AND `class <> ''`. The `not_open` and `unclassified` counts in the note exist precisely so the operator can reconcile this panel against the Findings table and against a report that includes exploited findings. Both are 0 on the demo, so the reconciliation is not exercised there — construct a finding with status='exploited' to test it.
USES A PRIVATE NAME. `audit._ORDER` is underscore-prefixed. ui.py already reaches into audit for `llm_coverage` (ui.py:2078), but importing `_ORDER` is a new private coupling. Either promote it to `FAMILY_ORDER` in audit.py (one-line rename plus its two uses) or accept the coupling knowingly.
BEST-EFFORT, LIKE ITS SIBLING. Wrapped in `try: ... except Exception: return ""` so a malformed `class` value can never break the 3s poll — the same pattern as ui.py:2078-2081 and ui.py:1104-1106.
SCALE: constant at 2,902/2,904 B. Seven rows always; only the `ids` list can grow, and it is capped at 8 ids per family with a "+N" tail. A 256-host estate renders the same seven rows.
IDS ARE DISTINCT CLASS VALUES, NOT COUNTS PER ID. `CWE: 51 finding(s) / CWE-200` means 51 findings across 1 distinct class. If a per-id breakdown is wanted, that is the Findings table's `class` column, not this panel.

  FROM finding
 WHERE engagement_id = ? AND COALESCE(class, '') <> '' AND status = 'open'
 GROUP BY class

SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finding WHERE engagement_id = ?1
     AND status = 'open') AS open_total,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finding WHERE engagement_id = ?1 AND status = 'open'
     AND COALESCE(TRIM(class), '') = '') AS unclassified,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM finding WHERE engagement_id = ?1
     AND status <> 'open') AS not_open
